text: The vertex is decomposed into Dirac and Pauli form factors. Sandwiching the nonlocal tree vertex between external spinors and applying the Dirac equation and Gordon identity gives F1 and F2, from which the authors use g=2[F1(0)+F2(0)].

The one-loop vertex calculation replaces internal propagators and vertices by nonlocal counterparts, introduces Feynman parameters and a shifted loop momentum, and expands the exponential factors in inverse nonlocality scales. Gamma-matrix reductions and Wick rotation evaluate retained finite pieces.

Bounds are inferred by requiring the leading positive nonlocal contribution not to exceed the quoted muon discrepancy or electron experimental uncertainty. Common-scale mass ratios are then used to estimate electron and tau corrections.
Adds localized actions −∫√−γ s(φ), typically choosing exponential s. Also studies curved Einstein slices and changes conformal frame to simplify the tadpole equations.

Fixes transverse-coordinate gauges and reduces bulk equations through an auxiliary function f, including constant and hyperbolic-function branches. Glues bulk solutions using continuous metric/dilaton fields and jump conditions for their first derivatives.
Separate the Klein–Gordon and covariant Dirac equations into radial wave problems. The spinor equations produce partner potentials V_±=W²±dW/dr_*, with W=m√f/r.

Compute time profiles by characteristic integration in double-null coordinates and extract frequencies with Prony fitting. A separate Frobenius implementation supplies an author-reported scalar-spectrum comparison.

Derive an entropy bound by lowering a finite-size object toward the horizon and applying the first and generalized second laws. Estimate the divergent scalar thermal-atmosphere entropy with WKB mode counting and the brickwall method.

Computes sublattice cell-volume ratios using determinants after mapping the full operator-charge lattice to an integer basis. This measure is invariant under changes of lattice basis and simultaneous invertible linear transformations, including current rescaling.

Uses discrete projections, BPS charge vectors and chiral-ring information to compute protected-sector indices. Tests a possible obstruction to convexity by seeking non-BPS small-charge operators collinear with higher-charge BPS operators.

In two dimensions, combines Sugawara charge-dimension bounds with spectral flow from the vacuum. Spectral flow preserves saturation and generates a lattice of operators with minimal dimension at their charges.

Calculate the one-loop graviton propagator using spin projectors, approximate logarithmic factors by small anomalous powers, and Fourier transform through Euclidean momentum integrals to equal-time spatial correlators and power spectra.

Propagate the primordial tensor spectrum with a standard gravitational-wave transfer function, assuming Einstein behavior by horizon re-entry. The thermal history has no inflationary reheating and is compared to instantaneous reheating at the Planck temperature.

Relate early density correlators to metric correlators through linearized quantum equations. Connect density perturbations to the last-scattering potential with the Einstein Poisson equation, then use Sachs–Wolfe and curvature-perturbation relations.

Compares calculated evaporation with compiled abundance constraints. The 511 keV proposal uses a first-approximation rescaling of a published 4D analysis while holding the local PBH number density fixed.

Uses semiclassical Schwarzschild Hawking emission, geometric-optics absorption and constant greybody factors normalized to the emitting area seen by SM fields: Γ_s=1, approximately 2/3 and 1/4 for spins 0, 1/2 and 1. Thermal particle and power integrals use Gamma/zeta identities; integrated mass loss supplies lifetime estimates.

Find mapping-class-group fixed surfaces, then invariant maximal isotropic lattices. Detect anomalies by transforming one-form backgrounds and extracting the Heisenberg normal-ordering phase. Higher-genus examples use polygon isometries and finite-field Jordan decomposition.

Use the discrete-flux Heisenberg algebra, its normal-ordering phase, and Stone–Neumann–Mackay representations. A maximal isotropic lattice selects conformal blocks and a topological boundary condition; changing that lattice changes the lower-dimensional global structure.

Cancel the anomaly of a gauged one-form background by stacking a minimal three-dimensional TFT on the zero-form defect. For noncoprime anomaly coefficient p and group order N, the paper reduces to an anomalous Z_(N/d) sector after gauging the anomaly-free Z_d subgroup, where d=gcd(N,p).

Reviews conformal lifting of a sufficiently dense collection of past-incomplete maximal causal geodesics, followed by extensions of the lifted curves into earlier epochs. This is a formal construction whose physical interpretation requires additional assumptions.

Conceptual comparison of generalized cosmic censorship with ordinary cosmic censorship and trans-Planckian censorship, focusing on whether anticipated UV physics constrains effective descriptions or is screened from cosmological phenomenology.

Constructs an illustrative extension of the top half of two-dimensional Misner spacetime by gluing suitably smoothed, oppositely oriented truncated copies. A sufficiently narrow region containing two Cauchy-horizon components can disappear from an insufficiently delicate coarse-grained metric.

The mechanics discussion uses Legendre-dual generating functions, Hamilton–Jacobi equations, Schwarzian derivatives, and a cocycle condition. Higher-dimensional extensions use quadratic identities together with continuity equations.

Worldsheet model classification uses free-fermion boundary-condition basis vectors, generalized GSO projection phases, and one-loop partition functions. A bosonic orbifold presentation makes discrete torsion and Wilson-line background data explicit.

Numerically integrates the multifield background in e-fold time and coupled linear field/metric perturbations, using Bunch-Davies initial conditions to obtain the curvature spectrum. Inflationary observables are evaluated near k*=0.05 Mpc^-1.

Computes PBH collapse fractions from the Gaussian overdensity tail, with variance obtained by smoothing the scalar spectrum; converts wavenumber to PBH mass and integrates the mass-dependent abundance over logarithmic mass.
Calculates radiation-era scalar-induced gravitational waves through second-order tensor perturbations, using a convolution of two scalar power spectra with radiation-era kernels.

Solve the radial warped Laplace eigenproblem with Neumann conditions at both throat ends and the stated normalization ∫|χn|²dy=1. An assumed one-dimensional KK tower is also used for one-loop matching to the tree-level field-space metric.

Integrate the warped KS volume up to yUV, impose negligible warping at the bulk junction and require the throat volume to remain below the total warped volume. Compatibility of the resulting radial bounds supplies the volume constraint.

Use a warped Kähler-potential expansion, leading modified no-scale cancellations, F-term racetrack stabilization and the inverse-Kähler-metric Hessian to estimate masses. Numerical searches stabilize S and T together after analytically stabilizing Z.

Average products of random phases to calculate charge-sector and total purities, then express second Rényi curves through those averaged purities. Sector dimensions in the qubit example are binomial coefficients.

Obtain leading thermodynamic expressions from sector dimensions and evaluate finite-N examples. For symmetry breaking, separate charge-block-diagonal and charge-block-off-diagonal contributions and study a Gaussian family of sector weights.

Euclidean replica partition functions relate modular free energy to Rényi entropy. The calculation imports Cardy state counting and Carlip's Gaussian correction; a separate large-q treatment uses an inherited classical Liouville truncation onto the defects.
Barnich–Brandt–Compère covariant surface charges evaluated on horizon-preserving Carlip–Silva generators; their centrally extended charge algebra is promoted to a quantum Virasoro algebra.

Use stationary-inflection conditions U′=U″=0 with a change in sign of U″, then deform away from exact stationarity. Potential slow-roll parameters, e-fold integrals and CMB amplitude/tilt relations determine benchmark coefficients.

Integrate Boltzmann source equations for inflaton decay and selected 2-to-2 scattering channels during reheating. Compare the resulting yields with the adopted present-day target YCDM,0≈4.3×10^{-10}/(mχ/GeV).

Estimate one-loop Coleman–Weinberg corrections using inflaton-dependent Higgs and fermion masses. Compare derivatives of the corrections near the inflection point with tree-level derivatives to bound reheating couplings.
Use charge conservation to remove φ̇2 at fixed q. For an action-level reconstruction, subtract qφ̇2 before substitution; direct substitution into the original Lagrangian gives the wrong force sign.

Expand φ1 around its shifted minimum, match powers of φ̇2², and substitute the response into the action. The operation generates nonlinear dependence on the light kinetic invariant under the stated adiabatic assumptions.

Normalize scalar velocities and potential energy by the Hubble scale and evolve in N=ln a. For varying slopes, also evolve φ1; Eq. (2.12) requires a normalization correction inferred from the definitions.

Integrate from fluid domination and from an observational crossing, then compare the histories. This separates a model's ability to accelerate from its ability to reach the observed epoch after the stipulated matter-dominated past.

Linearize the scalar equations around the evolving background and search for positive real exponential rates. The result diagnoses instantaneous scalar growth under frozen coefficients; additional evolution is needed to establish nonlinear fragmentation.

Relative Tomita operators, relative modular Hamiltonians and the Connes cocycle yield an approximate semiclassical density matrix. An imported horizon identity, S_gen(B)=S_gen(∞)-S_rel(Φ||Ψ_dS), connects its entropy with gravity.

Takesaki duality identifies the constraint-invariant algebra for unrestricted observer energy with the modular crossed product A_cr. Compressing by the positive-energy projection Π produces the finite corner ΠA_crΠ.

Noncompact gravitational constraints on states are implemented through coinvariants and group averaging, represented as top-degree BRST cohomology. Operators instead obey invariance constraints at ghost number zero.

For observed samples, generate mocks about the sample baseline fit, preserving the selected redshifts and errors or cropped covariance. Rank mock best fits to estimate directional tail probabilities. OHD/SNe tests remove low-redshift objects; QSO tests examine lower-redshift subsets of their higher-redshift baseline.

Construct profiles by taking the minimum χ² within approximately 200 parameter bins of an MCMC chain. Normalize exp(−Δχ²/2) over the sampled parameter range using numerical integration, then obtain integrated intervals with equal-height endpoints. These profiles supplement optimization-based mock comparisons.

Generate Gaussian H(z) mocks using DESI forecast errors over 0.05≤z≤3.55, fixed input H0=67.36 and Ωm=0.315, and four approximately equally populated redshift bins. Repeated fits construct distributions of best-fit parameters; input cosmological parameters themselves are not randomly drawn.

Organize divisor products in exp(Ĵ), Ĵ=φᴵD̂_I. Derivatives of Zφ=π_*exp(Ĵ) at φ=0 recover pushed-forward products. Pullback dependence factors as exp(φᵅD_α); the package omits this factor, which must be restored.

Represent classes in the ambient Chow ring, including the hypersurface class, and compose blowdown pushforwards with projective-bundle projection. Imported formulas use weighted substitutions E_i=g_i,k and H=−L_a.

Predefine a tower of dummy functions for partial pushforward compositions, then substitute the actual generating function recursively. Mathematica Apart[] and Cancel[] remove spurious poles during substitution.

Analytical tools include reviewed Landau–Ginzburg/Abrikosov physics, inflationary Nambu–Goto string production, and electric/magnetic dipole forces on moving vortices. Particle–vortex duality supplies an additional interpretation in 2+1 dimensions.

Abelian Higgs equations are evolved in Lorenz gauge on periodic domains, using fourth-order finite differences and Runge–Kutta integration, with constraint damping. A prescribed homogeneous axion source drives growth and is usually shut off shortly after vortex formation.

Reduce a homogeneous force-and-friction equation in a controlled slow-roll regime, derive the expansion rate along the trajectory, and impose interval-wide inequalities. The operation requires an independent background closure and does not establish a full covariant or perturbative theory.

Differentiate a positive scalar potential, compare its logarithmic slope with the small slow-roll requirement, and estimate the expansion accumulated over an allowed field interval. The finite-difference estimate requires control of slope variation and sign.

The scalar potential combines LVS, conifold/anti-D3 uplift, KK loop effects and higher-derivative F⁴ terms. Analytically guided constrained minimization uses SciPy SHGO; JAX computes gradients and Hessians.

The geometric scan imposes negative Euler characteristic, a diagonal del-Pezzo, K3 fibration, and coordinate-reflection involutions providing both suitable O3 loci and large negative D3 charge. Explicit analysis uses divisor topology, intersection data, tadpole accounting, and a local conifold expansion.

Mass eigenvalues in AdS units are translated into scalar operator dimensions through Δ(Δ−3)=m²R_AdS². For the two-exponential model, the vacuum equations are parametrized by α and the saxion expectation values, which the paper says can be solved numerically.

The author imposes D_iW=0 in the standard N=1 supergravity scalar potential, derives separate saxion and axion Hessians, and extracts physical masses using the inverse kinetic metric. The appendices supply the corresponding algebra.

A superspace construction decomposes a chiral multiplet into a part without an auxiliary component and a fully auxiliary constrained multiplet. Lagrange multipliers enforce constraints while integrating out the latter, generating an effective action with additional higher-derivative interactions.

Compute the s² contributions to twice-subtracted forward 2→2 amplitudes, including elastic and inelastic goldstino channels and goldstino-scalar scattering. Dispersion-relation positivity is compared with sound speeds obtained from quadratic equations on time-dependent backgrounds.

Insert component solutions of superfield constraints into the chiral-multiplet action, then integrate auxiliary fields iteratively in fermion number. Quadratic-goldstino truncations determine propagation on scalar backgrounds; four-field truncations determine 2→2 amplitudes. Field redefinitions exchange redundant and three-point operators for useful four-point bases.

Use the Jacob–Wick total-angular-momentum expansion, Wigner small-d matrices and their Jacobi-polynomial representation. Partial-wave unitarity supplies nonnegative absorptive contributions; combining their different spin weights yields the spinning rules.

Combine contour dispersion relations extracting the coefficients of s in A(s,0) and t in A(0,t). The forward relation involves a difference of crossed cross sections; the two relations carry distinct residues at infinity, C∞^(s) and C∞^(t).

Study explicit tree-level Higgs extensions and channel-based four-fermion amplitudes, comparing low-energy matching with dispersive integrals and boundary residues. Translate selected coefficient relations into universal-theory oblique parameters.

Develop semi-analytic energy-leak estimates from integrated forward collision terms, followed by radiation redshifting to recombination. Use entropy conservation and ΓE(Td)=H(Td) in equilibrium, and quasi-static or frozen-in mediator abundances for short- or long-lived Z′.

Reduce annihilation, decay, inverse-decay, and elastic-scattering collision integrals using quantum thermal distributions. Regulate Coulomb forward scattering with a plasma mass; separate resonant production from contact contributions to avoid double counting.

Numerically solve coupled energy-density Boltzmann equations. The MCP calculation evolves SM and combined hidden-sector densities; B−L separately tracks SM, Z′, and νR densities, approximating Z′ as nonrelativistic during relevant energy injection.

Superconformal tensor calculus constructs composite multiplets and D-density actions. The gauge-equivalence program introduces compensators and extra symmetries, then fixes them to recover physical Poincaré supergravity.

For EFT diagnostics, classify seven types of matter-fermion couplings with the gravitino set to zero and organize derivatives of the composite function N. Terms with no compensator derivatives and matter derivatives acting only on U are selected to identify the strongest inverse powers of the bosonic composite F̃.

Promote periodic couplings to spacetime-dependent backgrounds, identify their anomalous variations, then gauge them. Compensating transformations of higher-form backgrounds and four-dimensional inflow identify the resulting symmetry structure.

Construct defects by BF-theory dressing and examine fusion with conjugate defects. Holographic calculations instead use Hodge dualization, asymptotic field expansions and renormalized boundary variations to extract currents and Ward identities.
Extend topological couplings to a four-manifold bounding physical spacetime. Independence of the extension imposes integral quantization and determines modified background field strengths.

Explicit examples use imaginary chemical potential and Fourier projection, regulated high-temperature free-field sums, RN Euclidean actions, and inverse-horizon-radius expansions combined with numerical Einstein–Yang–Mills integration.

Thermal-circle reduction and spurion analysis organize a derivative expansion in background gauge fields. Exchanging thermal and spatial circles relates the holonomy potential to twisted-sector ground-state energy and domain-wall tension.

Expand the near-identity Gaussian class function in characters using an approximate group-manifold heat equation. Characters obey Δχ_R=−c₂(R)χ_R; the delta-function initial condition fixes coefficients proportional to dim R.

CMSSM spectra are computed with Isasugra. For high-scale cases, heavy sparticles are integrated out near m̃, and uncancelled one-loop Higgs corrections are estimated with cutoff Λ≈m0(3); FlexibleSUSY and FlexibleEFTHiggs supply the relevant SM parameters.

For fixed benchmark contributions, vary µ and retain values yielding a weak scale inside the adopted ABDS window. Define Pµ=log10[µ(max)/µ(min)], the accepted interval length for a logarithmic prior; compare scenarios through ratios of these lengths.

Use minimization of the loop-corrected MSSM Higgs potential to predict the weak scale. For moderate-to-large tanβ≳5, use mZ²/2≈−mHu²−µ²−Σu_u(stop). Define ΔEW as the largest absolute contribution on the full equation's RHS divided by mZ²/2.
Thin-wall reduction gives a single dynamical radius R and action S=−π∫dt[2TR√(1−Ṙ²)+σR²]. Wick rotation and the zero-initial-energy bounce estimate tunneling from no disk to a finite critical disk.
The fluctuation determinant is not calculated. Dimensional analysis and translation zero modes instead estimate the rate prefactor per spacetime volume as proportional to (bounce action/2π)²/R_d⁴.

Jacobi elliptic functions describe static CSL profiles. For formation near a completed lattice, replace isolated-wall tension by the interacting-wall tension; a disk nucleated in a missing lattice site is used as a proxy for CSL completion.

Studies flux extrema through vanishing F-terms or equivalent flux self-duality: *G3=iG3 in IIB and *G4=G4 in F-theory. Organizes vacuum searches through sl(2), nilpotent-orbit and fully corrected approximations.

Uses nilpotent-orbit expansions, limiting Hodge filtrations, Deligne splittings and sl(2) weight decompositions. In one modulus, Π=e^{tN}e^{Γ(z)}a0, with Γ holomorphic and Γ(0)=0; weight data determine leading Hodge-norm scaling.

A proposed dimer partial resolution is tested by checking whether the adjacent gauge factors can have equal ranks. Fractional-brane and orientifold rank shifts obstruct the face fusion used to realize the dangerous resolutions.

Match the running coupling above and below each Higgs threshold, solve for the infrared confinement scale, and substitute it into the low-energy energy estimate. Sequential matching extends the operation to unequal VEVs while keeping M fixed.

Reduce the D equations using unitary canonical forms, paired antisymmetric singular values and phase alignment. The output is a convenient radial slice for computing Higgs spectra; global phase rotations require separate care when interpreting the full complex moduli space.

Construct invariants of one gauged SQCD factor before enforcing the remaining gauge actions. Epsilon identities, antisymmetry and odd index parity remove baryonic candidates in this application. The same operation requires a different output when M is even.

The analysis uses scalar–Friedmann equations and a separately conserved cosmic fluid, recast as an autonomous system in N = log a. Variables x and y encode the square roots of kinetic and potential energy fractions.

Seed estimates model a thermal de Sitter bath, approximate the rolling modulus locally by a massive quadratic system, and consider radiation from string networks or matter from primordial black holes.

Nonextremal zero-force loci are explored numerically and analytically in a charge-exchange subfamily. For SL(4,R), numerical examples are supplemented by a quadratic expansion around identical extremal solutions and a positivity analysis of its coefficient matrix.
Masses and scalar/electric charges are extracted from asymptotic fields, including an ADM calculation and a leading-order transformation to De Donder gauge for comparison with another normalization.
SL(3,R) extremal-force positivity is established by charge-angle substitutions that factor the force into a squared difference times a polynomial with positive coefficients.

Coherent-state-like soliton operators shift the field by a classical soliton configuration. Suitable proxy states are projected onto the lowest-energy exact state in their channel using long Euclidean-time evolution.

The first subleading semiclassical expansion is evaluated with point splitting, a vacuum mass counterterm, and vacuum-energy subtraction. Coincidence limits are taken after divergent terms cancel because local energy-density moments, rather than only total energy, are required.

Collective-coordinate quantization separates the soliton position X from fluctuations χ. Orthogonality to the translational zero mode constrains χ and its conjugate momentum; Green functions use the remaining bound mode and continuum spectrum.

Holomorphy, the prefactor's zero divisor, and line-bundle structure replace a direct open-string spectrum calculation. The uniformization relations ℘=X/Z² and ℘′=Y/Z³ connect homogeneous sections to the elliptic flat coordinate.

The M5 analysis combines divisor cohomology and the intermediate Jacobian with constrained extremization of the instanton superpotential, including Σ ai V(ei)=VE, before taking the shrinking-fiber F-theory limit.

In the orbifold model, the prefactor is extracted from the D3-induced correction to the wrapped K3 volume and hence the holomorphic D7 gauge coupling. The holomorphic torus Green function supplies the theta-function expression.

Finite-temperature effective potentials and numerical/analytic bounce actions describe nucleation. Composite production uses phenomenological string-fragmentation estimates and average properties of particle populations and their scatterings.

Relic freeze-out and entropy-dilution calculations include initially unequilibrated visible/dark sectors, BBN limits and long-range interactions beyond the Coulomb approximation. The unitarity appendix uses Legendre partial waves and S-matrix unitarity to obtain an optical theorem.

Cosmic-string spectra use numerical network evolution to determine loop formation, including particle-production corrections. Forecasts use integrated signal-to-noise ratios and power-law integrated sensitivity curves, with detector cross-correlation for LIGO.
Generate boundary data from a small-L, curvature-dominated approximate HJ solution, then integrate the first-order radial flow numerically, starting from the non-supersymmetric vacuum placed at r=0.

Reduce the radial equations to a constrained one-dimensional mechanical system, Legendre transform, and solve a Hamilton–Jacobi PDE for real F(A,X). The Hamiltonian constraint requires E=0; gradients of F generate first-order radial equations.

Expand F around the non-supersymmetric scalar extremum with warp-factor-dependent coefficients. Impose F^(1)(A)=0 to decouple orders; solve the zeroth order analytically, the second order numerically, and subsequent linear equations iteratively through order 15.

Boundary variation selects admissible boundary conditions. In AdS5, radial-gauge asymptotic expansions and the renormalized action identify sources, currents, and anomalous Ward identities, allowing comparison of bulk defects with boundary symmetry operators.

A heuristic constructive argument cancels the anomalous phase of a rational-angle symmetry operator by stacking the three-dimensional TQFT A(N,p). For p=1, the explicit five-dimensional defect uses N ĉ∧dĉ/(4π)−ĉ∧f/(2π).

Higher gauging restricts a ZN subgroup of the magnetic 2-form symmetry to an auxiliary four-manifold Σ4 with boundary Σ3. One sums over flat two-form discrete connections, imposing Dirichlet conditions on Σ3; the anomaly-free magnetic symmetry permits this gauging.

Direct radial integration uses elementary half-integer Bessel propagators, gamma and incomplete gamma functions, followed by hypergeometric parameter expansions using HypExp. Exchange results involve logarithms and dilogarithms.

Scheme changes isolate singular near-boundary Bessel-series terms. Exchange diagrams are reduced to ordinary three-point integrals and auxiliary integrals with one Bessel-K replaced by Bessel-I; the proof discussion uses analytic continuation, dominated convergence and Fubini's theorem.

Hybrid renormalization derives boundary amplitudes from the bulk at generic dimensions, then constructs local boundary counterterms involving sources and sometimes operators. Radial cutoff holographic renormalization is discussed as an alternative.

Intersecting solutions use a Killing-spinor ansatz with harmonic-function coefficients and the equivalent equation Γb(Daψb−Dbψa)=0 to reduce gamma algebra. Charges per unit p-volume are evaluated from Q=∮Γabcψc dΣab at transverse spatial infinity.

An imported limiting method constructs ψa=limλ→0 λ⁻¹Da(r+,r−)ε(r+,r−), where λ=r+−r− and ε approaches an extremal Killing spinor. Taylor expansion gives ψa=Waε0+D0aβ; different spinor extensions change only the displayed gauge term.

Nongauge character is tested using the necessary integrability condition D0[aψb]=(1/2)Ωabε̃ for a gauge-generated field, where Ωab=[D0a,D0b]. For the single branes, the author evaluates components with Ω0i=0 but nonzero corresponding gravitino curl.
Forecast detection through Iarray^eqv/B>Smin, using Smin=SEFD/[ηs√(npol B tobs)] and SEFD=2kBTsys/Aeff. Average pairwise spatial-correlation factors over the actual antenna or station baselines.

FAST analysis clips time samples relative to a minimum-variance reference group, fits a cubic background using ten neighboring frequency bins, adds estimated systematic and statistical variances, and profiles a Gaussian likelihood with background coefficients as nuisance parameters.

Solve coupled Maxwell and conductor-current equations at leading order in ε. Approximate reflector patches as oscillating dipoles, integrate their emitted fields over the dish, and numerically average the received flux over dark-matter velocities and polarizations.

Combine a nonlinear-to-linear variable change, a local limiting expansion, and an integral constraint. These checks test global admissibility and uniform approximation control independently of the separate action-variation mismatch.

Check a consequential reduced equation against the full supplied action in a tractable ansatz, retaining the volume factor and boundary terms. A constant profile checks normalization, while a nonconstant profile detects the derivative discrepancy.

Substitute gij = χhij into the vacuum tensor equation, trace over the three-dimensional indices, and identify the common separation constant. Remaining metric components still require their own equations.
Use a frame adapted to the fiber connection, retain its commutator coefficients in the connection and Riemann tensor, then separate total divergences before constructing the reduced action.

Integrate a specified profile-weighted vacuum-energy density, transform to Einstein frame, sum species with their signs, and expand only within the light-mass regime. The local-minimum analysis must retain the assumptions of the kernel and the profile.

Canonical Klein–Gordon quantization uses hyperbolic harmonics, hypergeometric radial solutions and a real normalization N_{ω,λ} fixed by the wedge Klein–Gordon inner product. Boundary limits are then compared with the proposed BDHM identification.

Null geodesics are solved using conserved Killing charges and the null constraint. Geometrical optics relates their direction to the frequency and hyperbolic-momentum labels of localized scalar wave packets.
Bogoliubov transformations compare global and Rindler modes. The authors examine large-global-momentum tails, energy/momentum smearing and stationary-phase estimates of the AdS overlap integrals.

Equivariant line bundles and gerbes are described through Čech data, connection-preserving lifts, bundle isomorphisms and group-cohomology constraints. Quantization and associativity determine which flat vertical gerbes exist.

Correspondence spaces exchange geometric and gerbe circle-bundle data. Genus-one worldsheet holonomies, Poisson resummation and modular transformations relate gerbe phases to shift orbifolds and test proposed frozen-singularity spectra.

Bosonized heterotic Narain CFTs describe metric, B-field and Wilson-line moduli through spacelike lattice planes. Circle momentum/winding exchange and lattice-vector Wilson-line shifts construct the conjugacy between two orbifold actions.

Start with a horizon-sized charged black hole, estimate pair-production discharge, and determine whether its evolution leaves the sub-extremal region. Apply the spectrum restriction only when the background persists long enough for this process.

Introduce the longitudinal scalar, transform it together with the gauge field, and recover the original massive-vector theory in unitary gauge. To compare with an axion-angle description, supply a separate normalization dictionary rather than identifying the two θ symbols directly.

Diagonalize the gauge kinetic matrix, align the reference electron charge using an orthogonal rotation, and express other states in the resulting canonical charge basis. Charge components include couplings, so their norm can enter the multi-field Festina Lente condition.

Solve connection compatibility, substitute conformal curvature identities, invert the trace locally, and define scalar composite functions. This is an imported reduction used by the paper; the printed tensor-curvature identity fails its contraction check.

At fixed n,V0,V1, invert ns(Φ) and r(Φ) separately, substitute into the potential ratios, and compare the plotted projections with observations. The paper uses this operation but does not print the inverses or preserve their branch restrictions.

Discusses Picard–Lefschetz contour deformation for oscillatory Lorentzian path integrals, and Markov Chain Monte Carlo studies of analytically continued path integrals in causal-set and triangulation approaches.

Reviews tensor-network and quantum-information techniques for holographic maps and entanglement/geometry relations, including spin networks as symmetric tensor networks and discrete-geometric realizations in loop quantum gravity and group field theory.

Reviews RG and coarse-graining implementations using auxiliary backgrounds, abstract counts of degrees of freedom, holographic bulk/boundary flows, and causal-set cosmological parameter transformations. These implementations supply a common language without being identified as the same construction.

Compute F-term supergravity potentials and Kähler metrics, then match the universal-attractor Einstein-frame potential and logarithmic canonical field redefinition. Kähler transformations enforce sequestering while preserving the metric.

Compare mass hierarchies and potential-gradient norms. For the proposed swampland extension, expand the potential in nilpotent terms, differentiate before imposing the goldstino unitary gauge χ=0, and evaluate afterward at X=X̄=0.
Rescale a nilpotent chiral coordinate by its nonzero holomorphic coupling, substitute into K and W, and compare the resulting coefficients.

Slow-roll background equations are organized as gradient flow for Q in an effective potential. Rather than specifying V(φ), the analysis infers the evolution of εφ from the scalar spectral tilt. The stationary-Q equation is also rewritten as a quadratic equation for Λ, exposing two solution branches.

Tensor sourcing is evaluated with Whittaker mode functions and a Bunch–Davies Green function, followed by constrained parameter exploration. Separate tree-level spinor-helicity calculations and angular-momentum projections give partial-wave bounds; external axions are treated as massless for high-energy scattering.

A linearized w perturbation on a fixed w=0 background is treated as an eigenvalue problem for q. Fully backreacted nonlinear solutions are then continued in amplitude and charge, monitoring the condensate and maximum Kretschmann scalar.

The authors solve the coupled stationary equations with Einstein–DeTurck gauge fixing, an AdS reference metric, Newton–Raphson iteration and finite elements. They report a nonuniform 200×300 grid and require relative error below 10⁻⁵.

The analysis maps the models to unitary-gauge EFT coefficients to assess scalar and tensor stability, then uses spatially flat gauge for scattering. Leading asymptotic interactions are expanded and the scalar fluctuation is canonically rescaled.

Optical-theorem reasoning supplies amplitude estimates, while the EFT four-point condition is imposed through Legendre partial waves. Tree-level contact and exchange diagrams are evaluated for Galileon four- and five-point scattering and beyond-Horndeski four-point scattering.

Estimate unstable-extremum lifetimes using a Fokker–Planck timescale, and discuss metastable-vacuum decay parametrically through Coleman–De Luccia and Hawking–Moss processes. Explicit tunnelling lifetimes are not calculated.

Weyl transformation to the Einstein frame and radion redefinition remove the nonminimal curvature coupling. The resulting potential supplies extremum locations and vacuum energies used to calculate Λc/H.

Solve the quadratic bulk-scalar boundary-value problem and evaluate its on-shell action, including brane contributions. Large- and small-radion expansions and numerical examples characterize extrema for three boundary-condition choices.

Take the BPS limit of the quantum statistical relation, subtract extremal reference potentials, and use the BPS first law to identify conjugate variables. Legendre transform magnetic potentials to obtain the ensemble with fixed magnetic charges and fluctuating electric charges.

Impose the BPS parameter scaling m→mε² and e^{γ_I}→e^{γ_I}/ε, then ε→0; additionally continue a→ia and t→iτ. In Einstein–Maxwell theory, expand the Euclidean metric near r=±a to determine the periodicity needed for regularity.

Apply the principle of symmetric criticality to the spherical metric. Factor its Weyl tensor as W=G·C, with C depending on metric components but not their derivatives, and use the trace equation to constrain pure-Weyl solutions.

Perturb Schwarzschild to first order in the GS coupling, locate zeros of the norm of K=∂t, and estimate temperature through Euclidean near-horizon periodicity. The entropy discussion then invokes an unchanged asymptotic mass and the first law.

Solve two independent metric equations using formal Frobenius-type series near r=0 and inverse-radius series at infinity, with z=1/r for the latter. For pure GS examples, choose a seed B(r) and integrate the resulting first-order equation for A(r).

Use null worldsheet contractions to establish the special control of exponential lightlike tachyon backgrounds. A separate genus-one partition-function calculation integrates the X⁺ zero mode and extracts an effective range −β^−1 log(μ_E/μ_*).

Transform to Einstein frame, introduce proper time y to the past singularity, and compare the metric, scalar and potential with local ETW scaling laws. The imported framework relates remaining spacetime distance Δ and curvature to field-space distance 𝒟 through Δ∼exp(−δ𝒟/2) and |R|∼exp(δ𝒟).

Compute large-tachyon field-space lengths and Einstein-frame spatial lengths, then examine constant large-distance contours of the combined dilaton–tachyon kinetic metric to describe stretched ETW boundaries.

Compute entropy using the Wald horizon charge, temperature from Euclidean regularity, and energy through the first law. Compare with Iyer–Wald charges including boundary terms and with the subtracted Euclidean action.

Use perturbative metric and dilaton redefinitions to replace the curvature-squared sector by the Gauss–Bonnet combination together with −16α(∂φ)⁴. In this string-frame representation the field equations are explicitly second order.

Expand the radial metric functions and dilaton to first order in α. Solve the static equations analytically, using hypergeometric functions in general dimension. For acceleration, reduce the dilaton equation to a PDE and integrate it order by order in A.

Constructs supergravity F- and D-term potentials, fixes Higgs gauge and phases, expands singlet functions in Planck-suppressed operators, and solves stationarity equations for the neutral Higgs components.

Uses nilpotency and additional superfield constraints to remove scalar, fermionic or auxiliary components. Higgs constraints remove Higgsinos and Higgs F-terms in unitary gauge; the inflaton constraint retains one real scalar.

Optimize obtained solutions by randomly changing one flux quantum by one unit, accepting only lower-Nflux configurations that again solve the minimum equations and retain a full-rank Hessian. Estimate instanton relevance separately by comparing perturbative and selected instanton-corrected periods along one ray.

Choose moduli near a stretched-cone tip and small upper-index flux quanta in {−1,0,1}; solve for the remaining fluxes, round them to integers, then solve the 102 real minimum equations with scipy.optimize.root. Retain solutions whose scalar-potential Hessian has full rank.

Use mirror symmetry and CYTools to obtain the perturbative prepotential from intersection numbers and Chern-class data. Encode the chosen stretched toric Kähler cone by Mv≥c and rewrite vanishing F-terms as a complex matrix equation involving period derivatives.

For each retained charge assignment, count charge-2 and charge-0 fields, repeatedly generate random superpotential coefficients, and attempt to solve ∂ᵢW=0. Compare the resulting SUSY labels with field-counting predictions.

Enumerate monomial exponent vectors through degree three; select N monomials whose full-rank charge equations uniquely determine N R-charges. Complete the superpotential with every allowed monomial, sort to remove permutation duplicates, and reject decompositions into decoupled sectors.

Uses conformally invariant three-point structures and melonic ladder kernels, selecting dimensions where a kernel eigenvalue equals one. Generic positive-spin parity-even/odd kernels are 3×3/2×2; corresponding scalar kernels are 2×2/1×1, with further reductions for odd spin.

Reviews the melonic Schwinger–Dyson propagator equations and inserts a conformal infrared ansatz to determine field dimensions. The full gap equations are solved analytically at λ=0 and iteratively numerically at λ→∞.

Combines numerical transcendental root finding, small-λ and d=4−ε expansions, large-spin/twist asymptotics, and a first-order melonic Feynman-diagram calculation to select a parity-odd higher-spin branch.

Dimensionally reduce Chern–Simons actions for membrane charges and DBI actions for tensions, treating membranes as probes. Calibrations and MMMS conditions identify fluxed bound states whose DBI expressions become perfect squares.

Expand massive-IIA equations and Bianchi identities in gs: solve harmonic, smeared leading equations, then construct localisation corrections using a three-form current K satisfying a Calabi–Yau Laplace equation. Tadpole cancellation removes its harmonic obstruction.

Translate flux quantisation and moduli stabilisation into quadratic Diophantine existence conditions; where exact D8 conditions fail, consider approximately aligned flux with a small primitive remainder.

Vary the proposed superpotential with respect to the dilaton, RR potentials, bispinors and B-field. Integration by parts and decomposition into G2 representations relate these variations to the pairing equation and the remaining bispinor equations.

Use the imported reformulation of Killing-spinor conditions as bispinor polyform equations, supplemented by RR Bianchi identities to obtain supersymmetric solutions of the ten-dimensional equations of motion. Local sources enter directly through the Bianchi identities.

Expand toroidal forms and fluxes in dual three-/four-form bases, reduce supersymmetry to algebraic equations, and investigate flux-scaling symmetries subject to source tadpoles. A symmetry-reduced flux choice supplies an explicit solution.

Develops matter-surface bookkeeping with χβ=∫S(β)G4vert and S(β)=S0(R)+biDi|CR, summing contributions to each daughter representation. Bulk adjoint matter uses S0=0 and CR replaced by KΣ. Root-lattice embeddings and an explicit E6 resolution supply group and intersection data.

Uses the imported intersection-theory framework: quotient redundant divisor-product surfaces by null vectors of their intersection matrix to obtain Mred, then express integrated fluxes, symmetry constraints and chiral indices through linear algebra.

Evaluate the perturbative Repulsive Force Condition, including scalar attraction, for candidate charged string excitations. Separately count KK species using N∼k^n for n decompactifying dimensions and Λsp²=MPl²/Nsp to compare gravitational and string scales.

Classify homogeneous divisor-volume limits using effective, movable and Kähler cones, intersection numbers and compensating co-scalings. Cosmic-string backreaction identifies the suppressed instantons and corresponding D3-string charges; toric examples illustrate chamber dependence.

Harmonic-form dimensional reduction, orientifold truncation and Weyl rescaling construct the four-dimensional EFT. The F-term potential and Euler identities for homogeneous internal volumes are used to constrain runaway slow roll.

A Lagrange multiplier and algebraic elimination dualize the four-form. Clockwork mass-matrix eigenvalues determine the ultralight mode; supersymmetric type IIA F-term relations are used to test whether a required null eigenvector exists.

Bogoliubov transformations between specified in/out vacua give occupation numbers Nk=|βk|². Hankel/Bessel asymptotics and momentum integration estimate energy production at each tower level and its accumulated cosmological effect.

Use the leading high-temperature free energy F=(a0+a2 g²)T⁴, with a0<0, a2>0 and g²=κ/σ. Define the static critical temperature by Vtotal′=Vtotal″=0 and locate the corresponding critical field numerically.

Solve the noncanonical modulus equation and Friedmann equation together with radiation evolution. For continuous reheating, also evolve oscillation-averaged inflaton and radiation energy densities, scanning initial modulus positions to locate the two overshooting thresholds.

Use a constrained Legendre transform of the supersymmetric action, homogenized to degree one; real entropy selects imaginary Lagrange-multiplier roots. Separately solve algebraic near-horizon correction equations for equal rotations and evaluate Wald entropy.

Evaluate the first-order correction on the uncorrected saddle at fixed boundary sources. Differentiate the non-supersymmetric grand-canonical action to obtain thermodynamic quantities, then approach the BPS locus with q fixed to its BPS value and r+ = r* + epsilon.

Eliminate auxiliary fields in standard-Weyl off-shell N=2 supergravity using their leading-order solutions, then simplify the action through field redefinitions, integrations by parts and curvature identities. Holographic counterterms renormalize the Euclidean action.

Parameterize axionic dark radiation through hidden/visible decay fractions and relativistic degrees of freedom, then derive the visible reheating temperature. Numerical exclusions use the paper's historical Planck 2018 bounds and its fit to cited Fermi-LAT annihilation limits in the bb̄ channel.

Canonicalize the separable logarithmic Kähler metric through exponential field redefinitions, then rotate orthogonally into the volume eigenmode φV and transverse eigenmode φu. Expand kinetic and matter terms to obtain modulus couplings and decay widths.

Construct conformal maps to a portion of the Einstein static universe to identify causal boundaries and Penrose diagrams. Radial-null expansion determines the apparent horizon, whose area supplies an entropy-capacity bound.

Review O(4)-symmetric Euclidean Hawking-Turok solutions, analytically continue to an open universe, and excise the singular region using domain-wall regulators. Estimate nucleation likelihood using a regulated Euclidean action and the tunneling prescription.

Solve the homogeneous scalar and Friedmann equations using a constant-equation-of-state attractor. Review its scalar and tensor spectra, then compare classical scalar displacement over a Hubble time with the quantum fluctuation to locate self-reproduction.
Combines a previously reported approximate analytic and numerical localized-KK spectrum with uplift-energy scaling, discrete flux-spacing estimates, and LVS mass power counting.

Uses imported near-conifold periods, a flux superpotential, and a warped N = 1 effective Kähler potential for Z and V. The paper states and applies earlier results rather than deriving this effective action.

Homological AHSS starts from E²_{p,q}=H_p(X;Ω_q^ξ(pt)); cohomological AHSS starts from E₂^{p,q}=H^p(X;K^q(pt)), or KO coefficients. Its limiting page determines an associated graded group, requiring separate extension information. Negative q must be retained for K-theory and Bott periodicity.

The calculations use universal coefficients, split forgetful maps, edge homomorphisms forcing certain differentials to vanish, and Ext classifications of extensions. Appendix A proves sphere and torus bordism decompositions by suspension, wedge splitting, and induction.

Analyze extrema of the corrected potential in the two shape parameters (gsM,p/M). Translate selected bounds into illustrative LVS tadpole requirements using the imported Parametric Tadpole Constraint and uplift matching.

Evaluate tangent and normal curvature invariants, including second-fundamental-form terms, in a spherical parametrization of the deformed conifold. Integrate the proposed NS5 curvature action over its wrapped S2 to obtain the potential correction.

For p=1, decorate an interface with the three-dimensional action N a∧da/(4π)+a∧dA/(2π). Its equations of motion give a θ jump of −2π/N. General p uses the minimal AN,p TQFT describing Hall filling p/N, composed with naive time reversal.

An alternative construction gauges discrete magnetic one-form symmetry in half of spacetime. With pk=1 mod N, combine discrete gauging and counterterm operations with K; the authors use this construction to establish topologicity and conservation and derive condensation-defect fusion.

Analyze background-field transformations and five-dimensional anomaly inflow, then evaluate discrete gauging of quadratic one-form SPT actions. Cup products and Pontryagin squares distinguish odd/even N and bosonic/fermionic cases.

Compute object fusion by stacking and decomposing vacuum pairs into symmetry orbits. An explicitly imported theorem identifies K₀(2Rep(G)) with a twisted Burnside ring: double cosets determine stabilizer intersections, with restricted and conjugated cocycles supplying the twists.

Encode symmetry on an n-vacuum 2d TQFT through monoidal functors into Mat_n(Vec). Identify its boundary conditions with a finite semisimple category and use symmetry actions, module categories and projective representations to describe interfaces.

Proposed-defect fusion uses gcd/lcm exact sequences for gerbes, a box Σ×I whose path integral identifies boundary bundles through parallel transport, and finite-group twisted-sector counting before shrinking I.
Character sums construct orthogonal universe projectors. The universal coefficient and Hurewicz theorems identify the relevant matching-degree theta-angle group with Hom(K,U(1)).

BF worldvolume actions, background two-form fields, and bulk gauge transformations diagnose symmetry obstructions. In the Z2 fusion example, Φ1−Φ2 becomes gauge invariant and permits B1=−B2. Topological line junctions provide a complementary operator description.

Stabilizer induction, Shapiro's cohomology isomorphism and a Mackey-type double-coset decomposition translate orbit data into subgroup/SPT data and organize fusion. Subgroups are considered up to conjugacy, and restrictions of cocycles to subgroup intersections are sometimes implicit.

Junctions are described by graded projective representations, equivalently equivariant vector bundles with projective action. Folding relates arbitrary surface junctions to junctions from the identity; composition contracts intermediate gradings and fusion uses tensor products.

Operational gauging sums networks of symmetry defects. The algebra object A = ⊕g∈G g ends on candidate surfaces through left/right actions, supplemented by invertible local operators and compatibility conditions ensuring topological invariance.
Use f(H)=F′(H), g(H)=HF′(H)−F(H), the vacuum constraint Φ̇²+g(H)=0, and the Hubble equation to eliminate Φ̇. For f′≠0, express Ḣ and Ḧ in terms of H and Taylor-expand around H0.

Interpret the first nonzero nonlinear Hubble perturbation as motion in an effective potential. Separately expand the denominator-degenerate case f′(H0)=0 and examine an imported sine-function example.

Introduce O(d,d)-compatible matter source variations and a continuity equation. For V(Φ), derive a constrained dilaton evolution equation; inspect selected negative polynomial and exponential potentials numerically and treat a quadratic example analytically.

Split the F-term potential into perturbative, nonperturbative, and mixed pieces; calculate symbolically in Mathematica and expand at large volume. Stabilize τ1 through Dρ1W=0 using the approximate tree-level Kähler potential and a stated Lambert-W solution.
Add intersecting-D7 U(1) D-terms, transform τ2,τ3 to symmetric and antisymmetric fields, minimize the latter, and inspect illustrative parameter choices for the resulting single-field potential.

Use the N=1 F-term potential with K=−2ln(V+ξ+ηlnV) and W=W0+Ae^(−ατ1), after suppressing other nonperturbative exponentials. The perturbative ingredients are an α′³ contribution and logarithmic corrections associated with localized gravity and D7/O7 exchange effects.
Reduce D5/D7 Wess–Zumino anomaly polynomials to defect actions. Analyze polarization using a truncated non-Abelian DBI action and static matrix solutions proportional to su(2) generators.

Treat the radial direction as Hamiltonian time. Vary nondynamical time components to obtain Gauss constraints, exponentiate singular gauge transformations, and introduce auxiliary three-dimensional fields when a genuine boundary operator cannot be obtained by direct integration by parts.

Obtain bulk topological couplings by reducing the supergravity anomaly form I11 = ½F5 dF5 − F5 H3 F3 on T¹,¹, or through consistent truncation. Dualize c0 to c3 with a Lagrange multiplier; matching the displayed action also requires total derivatives.

Hamiltonian quantization of twisted Maxwell theory gives electric/magnetic torsion-flux commutators with phase (−1)^(α·β), represented by a Z2 gauge theory. Fusion is then evaluated by changes of path-integral variables and Poincaré duality.

Reduce brane Wess–Zumino couplings and sum over worldvolume gauge fields, retaining induced lower-dimensional brane charges. The full dynamical brane is proposed instead of a bare supergravity holonomy, motivated partly by K-theoretic charge quantization.

Twisted differential cohomology tracks flat torsion classes, cup products and perfect linking pairings. A central normalization is ∫RP5 ŭ2 ⋆ ŭ4 = 1/2 mod 1; background fluxes are expanded using the twisted generator t̆1.

Average neutral-state two-to-two scattering over a Boltzmann velocity distribution and perform χ² fits to imported halo-inferred cross sections. Near threshold, s−mS²≈m²(8δ+v²); the double-pole term dominates, with coefficient σ2=8y⁴/(πNf²m²).

Expand the ADS superpotential and tree-level meson Kähler potential around the supersymmetric vacuum, canonically normalize fields, and calculate one-loop wavefunction corrections through fermion self-energies. The appendix includes Kähler-metric Christoffel contributions to Yukawa couplings.
Uses imported conformal crossing, double-trace spectra, Ward identities, and conformal-block orthogonality to identify the stress-tensor obstruction to generalized-free-field factorization.
Uses saddle-point partition-function asymptotics and coherent-state descriptions. Comparisons across changing N first reduce predictions to invariant observables with an N-independent measure.
Uses the Fisher metric as a divergence Hessian, the Fubini–Study pullback for quantum states, and integrated connected Euclidean two-point functions for QFT vacuum metrics.

Bootstrap relative vacuum-dependent wormhole factors by requiring cancellation separately for each connected component. A cyclic phase S obeys Sᵏ=1 and Σᵢ₌₀ᵏ⁻¹Sⁱ=0; an n-boundary connected component acquires the corresponding sum raised to n−1.

Introduce replica collective fields G and Lagrange multipliers Σ, rotate integration contours, solve the large-N saddle equations, and sum saddle phases. The fixed-coupling interpretation relies on an imported near-saddle self-averaging comparison using four replicas.

Authors calculate slow-roll parameters, e-folds, ns and r, then describe eliminating φ from observable expressions to express swampland coefficients through ns or r. Compatibility is assessed using selected parameter values and plotted constraints.
The setup uses the scalar equation, traced gravitational field equation and an imported conserved-current construction to relate the coupling, Brans–Dicke function and potential.

Model finite horizon variables by cutting off spinor-bundle Dirac eigensections and quantizing their coefficients as fermionic oscillators. Matrix bilinears and polynomial Hamiltonians provide fuzzy approximations to area-preserving dynamics and candidate nonlocal scrambling systems.

Use semiclassical black-hole entropy deficits and infall entropy increases to motivate localized energy as constraints on horizon variables. Interpret Einstein equations as hydrodynamics, then construct quantum evolution matching a chosen FRW entropy and energy-density scaling.

Reduce linearized near-horizon Einstein dynamics to a Liouville-type theory; assume a quantum Virasoro representation with L0 bounded below and apply Cardy counting. The reviewed argument associates central charge with transverse area and motivates a universal modular-energy fluctuation formula.

Dimensional reduction tracks radion dependence of potentials and particle masses. Scalar charge-to-mass vectors ζ_i = −κ_d⁻¹∂_i log m organize towers into a convex hull; containment of a ball of radius 1/√(d−2) supplies a directional tower criterion.

The FRW calculation introduces dimensionless kinetic and potential variables x and y with x²+y²=1 and time dN=Hdt, then studies fixed points and late-time attractors. The appendix generalizes a reviewed four-dimensional exponential-potential analysis to d dimensions.

For multi-field potentials, the paper compares gradient-flow or kinetically allowed rolling directions with tower charge vectors. Type II tests inspect asymptotically dominant monomials V∼τ^(−n)ρ^(−l), rather than establishing the bound for arbitrary combinations throughout field space.

The inheritance arguments decompose higher-dimensional Ricci and Einstein tensors, restrict causal probe vectors to external directions, use positive-definite internal-metric contractions, integrate internal Laplacians for the SEC, and invoke closure of a common causal cone for the DEC.

For p-forms, a local Lorentz frame turns the measured energy density and SEC contraction into sums of field-component squares. Observer-dependent electric and magnetic forms, epsilon-tensor identities, and antisymmetrization are then used to establish a causal energy-flux vector.

Localized source stress tensors are obtained by varying distributional spacetime actions built from worldvolume embeddings. The orientifold analysis combines source charge cancellation with tension–charge relations for parallel D-branes and orientifold planes.
Solve the inequality for a, enforce strict parameter bounds, and check the original residual. Extend to a trajectory by intersecting pointwise intervals.
Transform the complete action, normalize the scalar kinetic term, and only then evaluate potential derivatives and asymptotic limits.
Infer potential-derivative diagnostics from scalar and tensor observables after restoring Planck factors and identifying the canonical field.

A finite-temperature scalar potential is used to characterize symmetry breaking. Action-angle averaging gives I∝a^−3 and, for V∝Φ^β, w=(β−2)/(β+2); quadratic oscillations therefore supply the matter-like epoch.

Imported transfer-function fits propagate the inflationary spectrum through intermediate matter domination. String forecasts use a scaling VOS loop model with α≈0.1, radiation coefficient Γ≈50, normalization Fα≈0.1, and only the fundamental j=1 mode.
Coupled scalar, radiation and entropy evolution equations are solved using ΓΦ≈fN²mΦ/(10π). Numerical entropy production is compared with an approximate analytic expression for the dilution factor κ.

Single-trace twisted moduli are located using G descendants of half-BPS primaries with h=1/2 and Q=±1. For twist L≥2, the seed labels must solve Σ_i[r_i/(k_i+2)−1/2]+c₀L/6=1, subject to the allowed minimal-model BPS spectra.

Conformal perturbation theory extracts logarithms from connected four-point functions with two modulus insertions. Ward identities reduce integrations to contours, and a covering map converts twisted insertions into seed-theory operators. Physical anomalous dimensions are eigenvalues of the resulting mixing matrix.

Products of seed elliptic genera remain quotients of theta functions. The authors apply a reviewed finite polar-state criterion: the maximal growth diagnostic α̃ is positive for Hagedorn growth and nonpositive for sub-Hagedorn growth. Nonpolar states need not be checked; the extracted detailed theta-function formula is not reconstructed here.

Use an open-system density matrix and Lindblad evolution, expanded in Hermitian SU(N) generators plus the identity. A distance-independent evolution matrix gives a matrix-exponential solution; diagonal QG dissipators permit an analytic oscillation formula, while off-diagonal cases require semi-analytic treatment.

Calculate primary-source fluxes by applying transition probabilities to source spectra. For secondary sources, integrate over parent energy and decay distance with an exponential decay law and a neutrino-production kernel. Appendix B relates the result to instantaneous primary emission.

Estimate perturbative inflaton decay into right-handed neutrinos and Higgsinos, derive reheating from their combined width, and generate a lepton asymmetry through out-of-equilibrium neutrino decay. Sphaleron conversion uses n_B/s=−0.35n_L/s; gravitino abundance estimates constrain reheating.

Introduce a canonically normalized field through the Kähler metric, modify slow-roll expressions using derivatives of that field, and perform numerical scans with slow-roll quantities treated through second order. An approximate curvature-normalization relation connects r to κ²(M_α/m_P)^4.

Construct global F- and D-term potentials and classify standard/shifted extrema. Along the D-flat shifted trajectory, combine the no-scale SUGRA F-term potential, Coleman–Weinberg one-loop corrections and gravity-mediated soft SUSY-breaking terms.
Background reconstruction: solve the mimetic Friedmann equations for V(t) and λ(t), substitute each H(N), and transform derivatives using d/dt=H(N)d/dN.
Calculate slow-roll observables using ns=1+2η−6ε and r=16ε. For the further-refined test, infer F1=√(r/8) and F2=(ns−1+3r/8)/2 in the slow-roll region.

Analyze generalized free theories using factorization, spectral representations and continuous-mass fields. Review the conformal OPE stress-tensor obstruction, extend the reasoning through a divergent stress-tensor correlator, and give a thermal argument for the central-charge species scale.

Obtain the static potential from the spectral discontinuity of the brane graviton propagator and its massless/massive tensor structures. Solve scalar–gravity backgrounds analytically and numerically; the ALD propagator uses an approximate piecewise treatment.

Project five-dimensional Einstein equations onto the brane using the Gauss equation and Israel junction condition. Decompose the effective stress tensor into Weyl, bulk-scalar and brane-tension terms, then impose the projected conservation law.
A Stückelberg decomposition separates helicity-0 and helicity-1 modes. The limit m→0, Λ2→∞ with Λ3=(mΛ2²)^(1/3) fixed identifies scalar Galileon and scalar-vector mixing interactions.
Transversity polarizations diagonalize spinning crossing relations. Kinematical singularities are removed using T+=[s(s−4m²)]^(2S)[T(s,θ)+T(s,−θ)], followed by subtraction of physical exchange poles.

Cauchy contour deformation and a Froissart-type bound produce subtracted dispersion relations. For spin 1, NS=6 and f is the sixth s-derivative of the pole-subtracted regularized amplitude divided by 6!. Definite and selected indefinite polarizations yield ten retained inequalities.

Compute local anomalies directly in BV superfields, incorporating ghosts and antifields. On a C3 patch, heat-kernel regularization reduces the one-loop quantum-master-equation obstruction to box diagrams with one distinguished internal edge.

Express the absolute value of the partition function through holomorphic Ray–Singer torsion, regard its phase as a determinant-line section, and use the holomorphic family index theorem to calculate the curvature obstructing gauge invariance.

Reduce the classical action along pseudo-holomorphic curves and integrate over CP1. Compare space-time loop amplitudes with tree-level axion exchange, then use polarization counting and holomorphic collinear factorization for the higher-point argument.
Reported endpoints come from graphs of two logarithmic sign functions. No numerical algorithm, precision estimate or independently inspected figure image is available.
Differentiate a potential, form residuals, remove positive prefactors, determine signs, and intersect the allowed sets. Canonical normalization is required before the physical test.
Transform the metric, extract the kinetic coefficient, integrate the canonical field, and rewrite the potential in that field before differentiating.

Evaluate the constant-radius Euclidean BPS probe action as area minus (D−1)/L times enclosed volume. For neutral solutions the stated result is SE=2πPLΩD−2 F(r), with F(r)=r^{D−2}√f(r)−(r^{D−1}−rh^{D−1})/L.

Determine the large-r sign after neglecting sectional curvature and the horizon-dependent constant. Supplement this asymptotic argument with reported plots of the toral five-dimensional action and its zero loci, including a mass/horizon scaling analysis.

Field stepping identifies trajectory endpoints; integration determines e-folds and the pivot field. Fitness combines penalties for insufficient e-folds, spectral index, tensor ratio and m*=(V*/ε*)^(1/4). Terminal states have f=0; spectral-index and normalization penalties use a cutoff f_term=−0.3.

Parameter values receive binary labels concatenated into a single genome. Polynomial coefficients use logarithmic discretization; argument coefficients of cosine and exponential terms use uniform discretization. The illustrated six- and ten-parameter searches contain 2^36 and 2^60 states, respectively.

The GA uses fitness ranking, probabilistic selection, one-point crossover and random bit mutation, with independent random restarts. Representative settings are population 100, mutation rate 1%, selection coefficient α=3 and 50 generations.

Use the hydrogen-like expectation value of r² to obtain the first-order shift δE = −4πmeρv〈r²〉/(3MP²). For n much greater than l, the leading shift scales as −ρv n⁴; positive density lowers the levels in this convention.

Fit energy differences relative to n = 22 with a modified Ritz formula retaining quantum-defect parameters δ0 and δ2, adding δE(n) − δE(22). Assess deterioration through χ²/dof and residual size and randomness; the authors report comparable unperturbed fits to the fuller Ritz expansion.
Adopt the Price–Romano Newtonian treatment with physical coordinate r = a(t)R and a heavy nucleus. The vacuum contribution gives V = −α/r − meΛCC r²/6, which is then used in the Schrödinger equation.
Derive the normalized flow, impose the Friedmann constraint, identify physical fixed points, and evaluate their equation of state and acceleration.
Match Bianchi terms to the potential's scalar weights, complete flux–geometry squares, and isolate the remaining geometric sign condition.

Dimensional reduction supplies scalar kinetic terms and potentials. After canonical normalization, inequalities aV+Mp Σ_i b̂_i ∂_i V≤0 with a>0 and nonzero derivative coefficients imply Mp|∇V|/V≥c, where c²=a²/Σ_i b̂_i². The authors use field-independent assumptions so the inequalities extend off shell.
Approximate the exact scalar–Friedmann system at small slow-roll parameters, express kinetic energy through the potential slope, and apply the acceleration condition.
Construct a sign-controlled off-shell inequality, normalize its scalar derivative direction, and use Cauchy–Schwarz to exclude positive critical points and bound the potential slope.

Combine the ten-dimensional dilaton equation, external Einstein trace, and full Einstein trace to obtain conditional inequalities R_d≤0. Sourced Bianchi identities, orientifold projections, completion of squares, and integration of total derivatives over the compact internal space supply additional obstructions.

For KKLT, use W = W0 + MS + Ae^(-aT) + Be^(-bG) + Ce^(-cG) + De^(-dG), with c = 2b and d = 3b. Split the scalar potential into KKLT and EDE pieces, suppress EDE cross-terms, and exhibit stabilization through potential profiles.

Decompose [1 − cos(φ/f)]³ into a constant 5/2 and three cosine harmonics with coefficients −15/4, 3/2, and −1/4. Generate these harmonics from separate leading nonperturbative effects rather than successive orders of one instanton expansion.

The supergravity toy model uses K = (G + Ḡ)²/2 and W = W0 + Ae^(-aG) + Be^(-bG), optionally adding SS̄ to K and MS to W. Evaluate the F-term potential and tune the two exponential terms and W0 to match the target harmonics.
Sample fast power-law tails or truncated logarithms, solve the constraint, and retain only globally admissible exterior geometries.
Use Einstein equations to obtain outward mass monotonicity, then compare its horizon and asymptotic values.
At fixed remaining couplings, lower a stabilizing coupling until the profile search produces a violating dataset.
Integrate the constraint, reject profiles with a nonspacelike exterior, compute mass and horizon area, and complete the data by gluing.

A frame formulation converts variations into flattened-index expressions for the vielbein, two-form, connections, H and dilaton derivatives. These variations are then used to impose invariance of the two-derivative Lagrangian.

Integration by parts expresses the deformation of L(0) through leading equations of motion. The variation of L(1) is decomposed into equation-of-motion terms and a total derivative. The b=0 case is computed first; H→−H relates the two first-order sectors.

The first-order calculation is organized by powers of composite fluxes ω, H and Dφ. Bianchi identities move terms between flux orders; a minimal leading form is fixed before proceeding to subleading terms.

A second construction starts from regulated disk correlators and determines the potential order by order in a fictitious parameter ε. Cylinder ribbon diagrams are classified and assembled from planar amplitudes, avoiding explicit knowledge of the complete potential.

Disk correlators are obtained by Schwarzian averaging of generalized-free-field Wick contractions modulo SL(2,R). Gravitational diagram rules use sl(2,R) 6j-symbols, orthogonality and Yang–Baxter identities; rescaled Wilson functions diagonalize the crossing kernel. The matter determinant is also expressed through a heat kernel and the Selberg trace formula.

A constrained ensemble squares a proposed operator relation quadratic in O and imposes it with a large coefficient Λ. The authors test planar Schwinger–Dyson equations using gravitational correlators; q-deformation regulates high-energy divergences that otherwise make intermediate unlacing manipulations formal.

For numerical work, derivatives and slow-roll expressions are rewritten in the original field φ because canonical-field potentials are difficult to obtain generally. The scalar amplitude fixes the normalization, while the thermal-history relation determines N* instead of simply assigning 60 e-folds.

The paper transforms to the Einstein frame and introduces a canonical scalar χ through dχ/dφ = 1/√Z. It gives Z⁻¹ = 1/F + 3(F′/F)²/2 for Metric gravity and Z⁻¹ = 1/F for Palatini gravity, with VE = VJ/F².
Potential slow-roll parameters yield ns = 1 − 6ε + 2η, r = 16ε and α = 16εη − 24ε² − 2ζ². Horizon-exit predictions use an e-fold integral, ending inflation at ε(χe) = 1.

Use polynomial equations from the perturbative prepotential, explicit factorization and duality transformations. For toroidal isolation tests, linearize all 11 equations in the 10 variables (τij,φ): rank deficiency is necessary for a continuous family, including possible off-diagonal deformations.

Impose λφ∂φW+λα∂UαW=0 as a functional identity with constant coefficients, solve its flux constraints, then impose F-flatness and additional conditions for flat directions. Filter by integrality, tadpoles, physical imaginary parts and, for tori, primitivity. The identity alone does not guarantee flatness.

For S8, the twist is built using an SL(9) subgroup, nine sphere embedding coordinates, the induced metric and a type-IIA seven-form potential. The resulting connection gives the SO(9) embedding tensor.

Substituting the scalar and constrained-scalar ansätze into the exceptional-field-theory potential yields a reduced potential expressed through the embedding tensor, up to total derivatives. The authors report a cross-check against upliftable three-dimensional maximal gaugings.

A generalized Scherk–Schwarz ansatz factors internal dependence through an E9-valued twist U(Y) and scale r(Y). Its Weitzenböck connection and shifted versions determine the reduced gauge transformations and embedding-tensor components.
M-/F-theory duality maps D3-branes on γ to M5-branes on the torus bundle T3 over γ. Mayer–Vietoris gives H1(T3)=Z⊕coker(ρ−1), providing ordinary torsion-linking data for the alternative reduction.

For nontrivial SL(2,Z) monodromy ρ, use cohomology with coefficient module (Z⊕Z)ρ. Quantize the mixed electric/magnetic fields as self-dual Maxwell theory, obtaining Heisenberg flux algebras and discrete Chern–Simons terms.
Dimensionally reduce brane Wess–Zumino couplings in differential cohomology along torsional boundary cycles. The D3 analysis retains the F̆1⋆F̆2⋆F̆2 term, which the authors identify as important.

Compare theta-dependent instanton phases with anomalous disconnected O(32) transformations; use D-brane Chern–Simons couplings and induced string charge to distinguish removable parameters from physical ones.

Analyze GL(2,Z) holonomy conjugacy classes with fixed axio-dilaton, project brane charges onto invariant fields, and follow S/T-dualities between perturbative descriptions. The claimed general conjugacy classification has an explicit proof gap in the appendix.

Reduce IIB fields on mapping tori, solving Wilson-line invariance modulo integral shifts through (ρ⊗ρ−I)A ∈ Z⁴. A D3 worldvolume mixed electric/magnetic one-form anomaly, represented by ∫B2∧dC2, determines induced string charges.

Use dual heterotic Wilson lines to preserve a gauge algebra while changing massive spinor sectors and global topology. Analyze lattice extensions of enhancement root lattices to determine which representations, and hence which central quotients, occur.

Distinguish primitive sublattices sharing an ADE root system by their extensions and associated global gauge groups. Use orthogonal complements in Narain lattices to propose charge lattices, and Mordell–Weil torsion and charge representations to track enhanced gauge-group topology.

Apply an imported Nikulin uniqueness criterion using AM=M*/M and its discriminant quadratic form modulo two. For the stated even unimodular ambient lattice, strict signature inequalities and rank(M)+l(AM)≤rank(L)−2 guarantee a unique primitive embedding. Cases outside these sufficient conditions need separate analysis.
LHC di-tau constraints are recast using MadGraph5, NNPDF23LO and a QCD pair-production k-factor. The treatment includes leptoquark exchange and destructive interference with the SM amplitude.
One-loop gauge RG evolution with Pati-Salam matching determines the intermediate and unification scales from low-energy MS-scheme inputs and the stated scalar spectrum in each interval.
SARAH 4.14.4 generates the model implementation for SPheno 4.0.5. R_D(*), R_K^ν and BR(Bc→τν) are evaluated separately using imported expressions implemented in local numerical code.

The authors import the Israel-junction thin-shell formalism and integrate the wall equation of state to obtain Ṙ²+Veff=0. After proper-time Wick rotation, the equation becomes Ṙ²−Veff=0; Euclidean solutions are classified using the largest simple or double roots.

Separate the massive scalar Klein–Gordon equation. Equal spins give an analytic angular separation constant; the radial problem uses Heun functions, ingoing horizon conditions and Dirichlet conditions at infinity. Mathematica supplies QN frequencies; τSR is the inverse maximum positive Im(ω).

Estimate Γ≈Ae^(−B) from the on-shell Euclidean action difference. Horizon terms are −A±/4 and the wall Lagrangian is −(σ−ΔP), giving B=−ΔSBH plus an integral. Wick rotation produces a complex metric; an optional a→ia continuation must subsequently return to real spin.

Set εW=1 to determine the endpoint, combine the Q–φ relation with this condition, solve endpoint values numerically, and evolve first-order equations backward to horizon exit. Compute ns, nrun and r across parameter choices; the principal plots use N*=55.

Use the imported thermal scalar spectrum and numerical enhancement fit G(Q)=1+4.981Q^1.946+0.127Q^4.330. Approximate tensors by their cold-inflation form, fix V0 through scalar-amplitude normalization, and obtain spectral tilt and running through logarithmic derivatives.

Primitive lattice embeddings, Weyl transformations and Dynkin-node deletion establish the Narain classification. Orthogonal complements and lattice genera, including the Kneser-Nishiyama method, organize orbit lattices and factorization isomorphisms.

Glue-code elements induce affine-Dynkin automorphisms. Root orbits are summed, with an extra factor of two when roots have nontrivial inner product. Current-algebra levels are assigned as 2m/αℓ², where m=nλ and αℓ is the longest root.

For non-self-dual charge lattices, gauge-group topology is extracted using coroot lattices and their overlattices in the dual charge lattice: π1(G)=W∨/L∨. Repeating this after node deletion tracks global topology under symmetry breaking.

LSS effective field theory, perturbation theory and galaxy bias expansions absorb unknown short-distance physics into fitted parameters, enabling full-shape power-spectrum and bispectrum analyses. Nonlinear scales require simulations including baryonic effects.

Formal methods reviewed include inflationary EFT and equal-time in-in correlators, the cosmological bootstrap, and EFT/diagrammatic resummation of de Sitter infrared and secular terms through stochastic inflation.

Axion abundance calculations use the homogeneous linearized equation ä+3Hȧ+m_a²(T)a=0 and m_a²(T)=χ_top(T)/f_a². Lattice QCD supplies low-temperature susceptibility; simulations treat strings and domain walls after post-inflationary PQ breaking.

Apply the cobordism hypothesis and higher Morita theory to dualizable point and boundary data. Local codimension-ℓ defects are morphisms from the tensor unit to the theory evaluated on a linking sphere; tangential and defect-to-bulk data govern globalization.

Finite quantization uses mapping-space correspondences and push-pull maps. Pushforward weights each fiber component by ∏_{i≥1}|π_i|^{(-1)^i}, rather than simply counting components. Semiclassical domain walls compose through homotopy fiber products.

Gauging replaces the regular boundary by an augmentation ε, giving the sandwich ε⊗σ F̃. Quotient defects perform this replacement on a tubular neighborhood, with Dirichlet-to-Neumann walls along its boundary.

Expand scalar fluctuations to quadratic order around a spherical monopole background. Construct radiation using its effective wave operator, retarded Green’s function and Bessel modes; evaluate the leading quadrupole at l=2, ω=2Ω for equal-mass binaries.

Numerically solve the authors’ modified TOV and scalar ODE system, imposing m(0)=0, φ′(0)=0 and φ(∞)=0, with central density parameterizing solutions. Stellar radius R50 is defined by a density decrease of a factor 50.
