Perturbative central-potential orbital analysis, explicitly integrable for p=5/6 (q=1), followed by quadrupole tensor-power calculations. General-p precession estimates use approximately circular orbits and nonlinear or quasi-linear asymptotics.

MSSV, implemented in Mathematica 13, derives orientifold-allowed scalar fields and fluxes, performs dimensional reduction, and constructs the scalar potential, kinetic terms and generic flat directions.

The consistency argument compares MSSV's four-dimensional extremum equations with MSSS's ten-dimensional equations up to linear combinations. Spectra follow from transforming the kinetic metric to canonical form and diagonalizing the mass matrix.

Numerically solves coupled Boltzmann equations for individual KK abundances, including brane production, decays back to Standard Model fields, and intratower daughter production. Early production also receives an analytic treatment using Bessel-function kernels.

Dimensional analysis of universal graviton–stress-tensor coupling estimates brane-to-bulk production. The expansion-compensated quantity y=ρKK/s gives production dominated by the initial temperature, conditional on approximate preservation of dark-sector mass.
Differentiate the field-dependent matter density, evolve the coupled background equations, and propagate perturbations using the imported synchronous-gauge system.
Compute cosmological predictions with modified CLASS, sample the joint likelihood using MontePython, marginalize parameters and compare best-fit likelihood and spectral outputs.
Subtract a reference angular spectrum and normalize each multipole by a cosmic-variance scale to display the size and location of spectral differences.
Integrate mass-dependent matter conservation, then change normalization to remove the explicit unknown present scalar endpoint.
Find one uniform initial lower bound and propagate its ODE comparison; positive initial minimum constrains smooth existence time.
Apply the gradient test to all coordinates of the object being tested; base-coordinate derivatives distinguish singular fibers from singular total spaces.
Cut out a framed product region, glue its complementary handle boundary and supply smooth caps before attempting to restart geometric flow.
Collapse the separating S³, compute wedge homology by Mayer–Vietoris, and use the relative boundary map to recover connected-sum homology.
Combine characteristic-class naturality, scale cancellation and degree-one integration under identity-connected diffeomorphisms.
Evaluate the velocity norm using the entire evolving background, then integrate in flow time; sector restriction changes the quantity.
Use the genus and ambient canonical intersection to compute self-intersection. The K3 simplification requires the resolved surface to retain trivial canonical bundle.
Specify a primitive elliptic polarization H⊕M to retain exceptional intersections absent from bordism; a definite ADE sector must have the negative sign convention.
Check a local approximation against the known scalar limit before using it to infer flow; pointwise metric agreement does not control curvature.
Replace a smooth complex point by its projectivized tangent directions while preserving the original space away from that point.
Construct exceptional projective directions and a blow-down map. Applying this operation to smooth points does not automatically reproduce crepant ADE resolution.
Solve for u and positive ξ, impose curvature integrality, construct the circle connection and assemble the metric; complete singular fibers separately.

Two entropy derivations use Connes cocycles: an approximate positive density operator affiliated with AR, and an isomorphism between crossed products constructed from different reference states. The latter requires preservation of the chosen trace.

The bulk identification applies Wall's imported relative-entropy argument and linearized Raychaudhuri evolution, ∂vθv=−8πG Tvv+O(G²), with future event-horizon expansion tending to zero. Trace-preserving entropy monotonicity follows from positivity of relative entropy.

GNS completion of limiting correlation functions, followed by weak closure/double commutant; adjoining the Hamiltonian realizes a crossed product by modular automorphisms. Centered alternating correlators similarly specify the free-product representation.

Use the primitive null charge of the tensor pairing matrix to contract Green–Schwarz coefficients into 2-group constants. Compare these constants, flavor ranks and circle-reduced Coulomb-branch dimensions across candidate duals.

For A-type examples, use Taub–NUT reduction and Type I′/IIB duality chains. M9 fractionalization gives M=N+Nµ1+Nµ2 NS5-branes, qualitatively explaining shifts between instanton-number labels on dual sides.
Assemble minimal M9–M5 orbi-instanton SCFTs and M5 conformal matter by diagonal fusion: K_N=T(µ1,g) ⨝g T_{N−2}(g,g) ⨝g T(µ2,g). Exceptional conformal matter is recursively fused from rank-one blocks.

For the Freund–Rubin vacua, linearized metric and background-U(1) perturbations are expanded in spherical harmonics. Coupled mass matrices are tested against the relevant Breitenlohner–Freedman bounds.

Field redefinitions f and ψ=exp(−f), together with a rescaled transverse coordinate ξ, reduce the background equations in the chosen sign convention to dψ/dξ=1+δ−δψ². Integration yields hyperbolic, critical linear, and trigonometric branches.

Scalar constraints reduce perturbations to one master equation, then Fourier transformation and field rescaling give HΨ=m²Ψ with H=b+A†A. Shooting numerics give orientifold masses approximately 0.97π/L and 2.13π/L; heterotic numerical instabilities prevented comparable precision.

Half-space gauging with Dirichlet boundary conditions uses relative cohomology. Fusion calculations convert cohomology sums into cochain sums with BF Lagrange multipliers and use Lefschetz duality to interpret the result as condensation.

EM gauging is treated through invariant operator combinations, twisted sectors and junction charges, and through explicit twisted-cocycle actions. In the (2+1)d dynamical-cocycle formulation, gauge transformations are restricted where the EM gauge field is not flat.
First solve continuity of normal energy-momentum flux for candidate sewing relations; then construct a defect Lagrangian whose variational boundary equations impose those relations.
Realize rational effective Chern–Simons coefficients using integer counterterms and two minimal 3d TQFTs A^{q,p}, with Z_q one-form symmetry, anomaly p modulo q, and gcd(p,q)=1.

Determine line actions through gauge-invariant monopole junctions and integral fluxes. For generic defect TQFTs, use folding and a 3+1-dimensional boundary realization to extract additional charge constraints.

GW standard sirens combine an amplitude-derived luminosity distance with source redshift. Bright sirens use electromagnetic counterparts; dark sirens can use statistical host identification. The distance calibration assumes GR, so the stated model independence concerns freedom from a cosmic distance ladder.

Cosmological neutrino-mass inference uses CMB lensing and the matter power spectrum P(k,z)=⟨|δm(k,z)|²⟩, together with clustering and weak lensing. Neutrino free streaming suppresses structure below its characteristic scale.

Dense-matter studies map an EOS to nonrotating neutron-star properties using the TOV equations; merger modelling instead requires the coupled Einstein and relativistic-fluid equations. GW departures from GR can be parameterized with post-Newtonian or post-Einsteinian frameworks.
Nilpotent-orbit approximations and commuting sl(2,C) triples from asymptotic Hodge theory organize periods, flux sectors, and allowed potential exponents near complex-structure degenerations.
Apply nilpotent monodromy to the periods, absorb axions into rho, and isolate saxion dependence in Z(s).
Minimize quadratic axion dependence in descending asymptotic order, fixing each stabilized combination before treating weaker terms.
Decompose the dressed flux by cumulative monodromy weights, then apply the orbit theorem to extract leading powers in an ordered growth sector.

The authors solve asymptotic gradient-flow equations using si(λ)=αiλ^βi, determine competing dominant monomials, and compute γ along the resulting trajectory. Polynomial axion chains organize sequential stabilization by subleading terms.
Optimize the largest monomial exponent, solve active-term gradient ratios, and validate the resulting runaway against its original asymptotic sector.
Compare Hubble damping with saxionic antifriction using the full integral, including borderline power-law cases.
Convert the asymptotic potential into term vectors, minimize norm on their convex hull, and compare the result with the four-dimensional threshold √2.
Order potential terms by asymptotic growth, solve the leading quadratic system, then analyze subleading restrictions on remaining flat directions.
Include connection terms before factoring the Hessian; positivity follows from its quadratic form, rather than from entrywise signs.

The scalar potential is minimized in the heavy-triplet regime using the induced linear term and quadratic triplet mass term. The CP-even doublet/triplet mass matrix is diagonalized to estimate Higgs mixing and coupling changes.

Axion-quality estimates use an imported Euclidean wormhole action; hilltop displacement constraints use a WKB approximation to axion dynamics. A proposed two-axion construction rotates to a heavy QCD-coupled mode and an orthogonal electroweak mode.

The paper gives the one-loop SU(2)L running shift and uses PyR@TE 3 to obtain two-loop RGEs. The resulting Planck-scale coupling enters the exponentially sensitive electroweak-instanton vacuum-energy estimate.

Equivariant BRST quantization includes ghosts for local symmetries. A Qeq-exact deformation localizes the functional integral onto Qeqψ=0 with gauge conditions; the vector-sector configurations are off shell rather than extrema of the original supergravity action.

The microscopic benchmark is an imported convergent Hardy-Ramanujan-Rademacher expansion involving modified Bessel functions of order 7/2 and Kloosterman phases. Gaussian integration over φ1,…,φ15 reduces the gravitational expression to one integral; topological action terms supply the phases.

Fields and ghosts are organized into cohomological complexes. The Atiyah-Bott fixed-point formula, orbifold method of images and zeta regularization determine index-captured determinants. An off-shell N=4 Weyl formulation supplies the N=2 spin-3/2 and chiral sectors.

A Källén–Lehmann representation connects nonzero zero-momentum TSV to a massless pole in the Chern–Simons correlator. The vacuum argument uses this pole rather than a particular instanton calculation; massive propagating modes are distinguished from their possible virtual contributions to TSV.

Dualization treats dB as an independent 3-form, imposes its closure with a pseudoscalar Lagrange multiplier, and integrates out fields. The resulting potential is V((a−a0)/fa), with an integration constant a0 retaining the original gauge/shift structure; K determines the potential through an inverse-function relation.

Computes one-loop beta functions and uses Hubbard–Stratonovich large-N saddle points, gap equations, free-energy Hessians and trajectory pullbacks. Distances integrate √Gvv along each selected RG trajectory and sum the steps.
Uses the Euclidean functional-integral information metric G=⟨(dW−dS)⊗(dW−dS)⟩. For parameters entering S linearly, the intensive metric is Gij=−∂i∂j w, with w=−log(Z)/Vol.
Pull the parent metric's phase restriction through an explicit reduction map, keeping induced scalar phases and external metric phases together.
Match a nearly de Sitter Euclidean cap to slow-roll expansion, then tune the initial scalar imaginary part to cancel the late constant imaginary component.
Legendre-transform f(R), rescale the metric, and normalize the Einstein coefficient. A consistent sign and inverse-map branch are required before interpreting the potential.

Recursive clipping identifies glitches using thresholds of 4.5σ against the moving average and 3σ in high-frequency-filtered data. The analysis masks one second before and 15 seconds after an outlier. Longer jumps lead to separate segments containing even numbers of orbital periods to suppress specified frequency contaminations.

M-ECM maximizes available-data likelihood by estimating missing samples through conditional expectations, using a circulant approximation to the complete-data covariance. It also estimates the noise spectrum and fills gaps. Adam provides a frequency-domain cross-check, while the analysis combines sessions to obtain the final constraint.

In-flight calibrations estimate off-centering, differential sensitivity and quadratic response. The frequency-domain Adam procedure iterates calibration, typically converging in two or three iterations. The corrected fit estimates a bias, δx gx, a quadrature δz gz term, and apparent off-centering terms Δx Sxx and Δz Sxz.

Pair production is evaluated with explicit helicity bases and initial-polarization averages at threshold. Appendices also construct interaction Hamiltonians for derivative couplings: additional vertices and propagator contact pieces cancel in the displayed nonminimal-coupling toy processes, supporting the rules used there.

The metric and matter actions are expanded through second order in gravitational fluctuations to obtain tree-level vertices. Elastic 2→2 amplitudes are separated into gauge, scalar, and spin-2 exchanges, then examined through nonrelativistic pole residues and effective contact terms.

An Einstein-Hilbert Hessian with perfect-fluid matter, harmonic gauge fixing, and a maximally symmetric background supplies the decoupling condition. With a mass-type regulator, k_dec²=G(k_dec)µ+γR̄, where γ=2/3 in four dimensions.

Iterative improvement rebuilds the cutoff from the corrected metric. Conditional on convergence, its fixed function satisfies a second-order nonlinear PDE for G∞(r,v), with generalized Vaidya energy densities and pressure depending on its derivatives.
Static limits use a small-radius power-law ansatz and a large-radius Stokes/Airy reduction. Evaporation uses Euclidean horizon regularity, T=f′(r+)/4π, and Stefan-Boltzmann mass loss dm/dt=−σA(m)T⁴.

Cosmological perturbation theory computes correlation functions and possible non-Gaussian signatures of additional inflationary fields. These calculations are related to scattering-amplitude questions in de Sitter, flat, and AdS spacetimes.

Reviewed black hole tools include microscopic state counting, quantum extremal surfaces, quantum error correction, out-of-time-order correlators, spectral form factors, and gravitational path-integral saddles. SYK supplies a solvable setting for parts of the chaos analysis.

Reviews geometric engineering, flux superpotentials computed through Calabi-Yau period integrals, and harder nonperturbative contributions. Numerical geometry and machine learning are discussed as developing tools for metrics and low-energy data.

Use reviewed anomaly inflow and discrete gauging to infer Postnikov constraints. Apply an imported construction dressing anomalous defects with TQFTs to obtain non-group-like fusion. Orthogonal anomaly assignments receive an additional duality-consistency test using ζ′=ζ and χ′=ζχ.

Compute fugacity expansions of the index using Cartan integrals and magnetic-flux sums in the gauge group's co-weight lattice. Fractional background fluxes reveal center-charged monopoles; fractional gauge-fugacity powers indicate inconsistent quantization. Discrete gauging obstructions diagnose anomalies, including indirectly after gauging a one-form symmetry.

A phenomenological mass-balance equation adds plasma accretion to Hawking evaporation. The local density required for accretion to dominate is compared with the average radiation density π²gε(T)T⁴/30 at selected cosmological epochs.

Higher-dimensional Schwarzschild thermodynamics supplies T_BH=(n+1)/(4πrs) and S=4πMBH rs/(n+2), with n=1 for five dimensions. The authors compare horizon and temperature scalings and use a graviton-bound-state identification to relate constituent mass to Hawking temperature.

At first order in the higher derivative couplings, evaluate the correction action on the Einstein solution at fixed temperature and potential. The background equations and vanishing boundary variation for q≥2 eliminate the need to compute the corrected solution explicitly.

Legendre transforms connect grand canonical, canonical, and microcanonical quantities. The canonical extremal relation dμ_ext/dQ=-G(0,Φ(0,Q))/Q² follows provided entropy and its charge derivative remain finite as T→0.

A semiclassical Euclidean path integral with fixed electric potential and periodic Euclidean time yields the grand canonical ensemble and Gibbs energy density G=T I_on-shell/V. The gravitational boundary action includes subtraction against flat space.

Dedicated lattice simulations are emphasized for strongly coupled gauge sectors, hadronic inputs, composite dark matter, and axion string/domain-wall evolution. EFT and scaled-QCD reasoning can guide these problems but do not supply definitive nonperturbative results.

Relic-density mechanisms are organized by number-changing reactions and their relation to Hubble expansion: freeze-out, sub-Hubble production through freeze-in, cannibal reactions, asymmetric populations, Sommerfeld enhancement, and bound-state formation.

Reviewed tools include EFT descriptions through symmetry-breaking patterns and partial compositeness, together with the FeynRules–UFO–event-generator pipeline for translating models into collider predictions.

Ultraviolet consistency methods include amplitude dispersion relations from analyticity and unitarity, nonlinear positivity bounds combined with crossing, propagation and scattering time-delay tests, and holographic translation of CFT or bootstrap constraints into bulk gravitational EFT bounds.

Enumerate light fields and symmetry-allowed operators, organize derivative or scale expansions, match heavy theories onto EFTs, and resum large logarithms with renormalization group evolution. Functional matching extracts the ultraviolet part of one-loop determinants through a symmetry-preserving covariant derivative expansion.

Specialized tools include NRQCD and SCET for annihilation singularities, statistical fluid-equation perturbation theory for LSS, doubled closed-time-path fields for dissipation, and staged integration of binary length scales in NRGR. Scattering amplitudes also streamline classical gravitational calculations.

Analyze higher-order stabilization by eliminating massive fields order by order and examining the remaining quadratic critical-point constraints. The procedure preserves the truncation order; solving truncated equations exactly can falsely remove a genuine deformation.

Solve linear supersymmetry constraints in an integral flux basis and search quantized configurations. For supersymmetric Minkowski fluxes, where W = 0 and A0 = 0, at τ = ω, quantization implies Nflux ≥ the number of nonzero Hodge-basis coefficients Aa, hence at most 12 such coefficients within the orientifold tadpole bound. This coefficient-count restriction does not apply to AdS solutions.

Evaluate Fermat-point periods and their Taylor derivatives using factorized elementary Landau–Ginzburg integrals. Superpotential Hessians can also be expressed through Yukawa couplings, avoiding reconstruction of the full moduli dependence.

Canonical normalization uses G=ΓΓ† and the matrix Q=Γ⁻¹(∂F)Γ⁻ᵀ. Singular-value decomposition reduces the scalar Hessian spectrum to functions of the nonnegative singular values σα and the vacuum superpotential.

For the no-scale sector, compute the trace of the canonically normalized mass matrix using complex-structure curvature and the Hodge metric. The inequality H≥2g relates this trace to flux-induced D3 charge and bounds the largest eigenvalue through the average eigenvalue.

Special Kähler geometry, periods of Ω and Yukawa couplings determine flux-dependent mass-matrix blocks. The DGKT mirror permits analytic diagonalization using directions parallel and perpendicular to Kähler-potential gradients; a more general minimal flux model is treated numerically.

Serre spectral sequences compute low-degree cohomology and Steenrod operations. The Adams spectral sequence runs over the full mod-two Steenrod algebra; an Atiyah-Hirzebruch argument excludes odd-prime torsion. Low-degree module decompositions and filtration constraints determine the degree-five bordism group.

Use the Freed-Hopkins classification and the Anderson-dual exact sequence to distinguish the free anomaly-polynomial quotient from torsion bordism invariants. Once perturbative cancellation makes the anomaly topological, replace the noncompact symmetry by its maximal compact subgroup.

Identify a geometric generator using the fourfold SU2 embedding into SU8, then evaluate fermionic anomaly phases through η-invariants and representation branching on the Wu manifold. Treat vector anomalies through oriented bordism and multiplicativity under direct sums of representations.

The review invokes the Riemann–Lebesgue lemma for suppression of distant off-diagonal matrix elements, numerical simulations for matrix structure, and Gaussian expansion calculations for rotational symmetry breaking.

Diagonalize A0 and order its eigenvalues. Define spatial submatrices centered along the diagonal at the corresponding emergent time, and use traces of their squares to define spatial extents and proposed physical lengths.

Thermal correlators are obtained from derivatives of the partition function: E=−∂β ln Z and CV=∂T E. Linearized Einstein equations relate density and off-diagonal pressure fluctuations to scalar and tensor perturbations.
Perturb ten-dimensional equations around the smeared SUSY solution using SU(3)×SU(3) structure, retaining the first localization-sensitive order.
Separate field dependence algebraically before extremization, or integrate out nonpropagating four-forms with consistent normalization and boundary terms.
Extract scalar charges from differential-form gauge transformations, enforce superpotential invariance, and contract the resulting moment maps with gauge kinetic couplings.

Pure-spinor equations and an expansion in average string coupling describe localized backgrounds. Wrapped D-brane membrane charges and tensions, including DBI/BIon corrections, diagnose possible decay channels.
Organize extremization through shifted flux polynomials rather than brute-force scalar equations; the supplied fragment does not yet specify the restrictions making the ansatz predictive.

Bilinear flux potentials separate saxion-dependent matrices from flux–axion polynomials. Polynomial derivatives and axion-independent flux invariants organize extremization into constrained algebraic equations; the formalism is extended to general fluxes and D-terms.

Hessian analysis uses canonical normalization and primitive/non-primitive metric decomposition, positive-semidefinite decompositions and Gram matrices; geometric non-SUSY stability regions are explored numerically.
Construct 4d symmetry defects by higher gauging subgroups of the bulk 2-form symmetry, with Dijkgraaf-Witten discrete torsion expressed through Pontryagin squares and a symmetric torsion matrix.

Use continuum defect actions and anomaly inflow to obtain 3d edge theories; analyze their line spins, braiding and minimal-TQFT factorizations. Fusion includes an extra braiding contribution from the dynamical 5d bulk.
Describe discrete gauging through a hybrid formulation: continuum 2-form fields on patches, a discrete simplicial 1-cochain a, and covariant gluing across patch intersections.

Split flopping from non-flopping classes and reorganize the instanton sum into group orbits. Expand Li3 in its multicover series; quadratic orbit exponents yield Jacobi theta sums. Elliptic fibrations are investigated through divisor criteria and configuration-matrix fibers.
For two generators, use S=M1 and Q=M1M2, with elements Q^kS^α. Explicit matrix powers and block sums distinguish finite-order, faster-growing and quadratic-in-k cases.

For Picard rank two, extract m1=2λ122/λ222 and m2=2λ112/λ111 from triple intersections. For higher rank, solve integer-vector conditions defining reflection matrices, then apply Vinberg’s reflection-group framework.

Constructs five successive blowups of the cubic presentation and analyzes fiber components in codimensions one, two and three. Intersections with section and Cartan divisors identify charges; codimension-three curve splittings provide geometric evidence for localized Yukawa interactions.

Matches geometric fluxes to one-loop 3D Chern–Simons couplings, including KK contributions, and inverts their dependence on chiral indices. Solves the symmetry constraints partly implicitly through A·H̄=φ34Σ2·Σ3−9φ03Σ2·Y−8φ05Σ3·Y, with H̄=−12K−4Σ3−3Σ2+12Y.

Uses Chow-ring pushforwards and an intersection generating function to compute quadruple divisor intersections. Forms M(IJ)(KL)=SIJ·SKL, quotients null directions to obtain Mred, and expresses integrated vertical fluxes as Θ=Mφ.
MCEvidence estimates scalar-model Bayes factors relative to ΛCDM. These model-selection results are reported separately from parameter agreement and upper bounds.

GetDist analyzes chains and marginal posteriors. All models use the full PL18+BAO+Pantheon+CC+RSD combination, with reported Gelman–Rubin convergence |R−1|<0.03. The analysis compares free-initial-field IDE, fixed-initial-field IDE, uncoupled exponential quintessence and ΛCDM.

A modified CLASS implementation evolves the background and cosmological perturbations. MontePython samples nine parameters: the six usual cosmological parameters plus λ, α and the initial scalar value deep in radiation domination.

Kaluza–Klein reduction of the NS-NS effective action; consistency of sourced Bianchi identities and equations of motion; Page currents and integral cochains to track charge quantization and gauge invariance.
BF-type topological couplings implement higher-form gauging. Networks of defects represent flat bundles; their intersections and fusion determine the resulting discrete gauge-group extension.

Associate graph integrals with relative periods of auxiliary algebraic families. Algebraic maps relate momenta and masses to geometric parameters; resolution of singularities and homogenization enter the construction. Apply the imported definability theorem for relative periods.

Treat dimensional regularization through deformed GKZ differential systems and their Laurent/Frobenius expansions; invoke BPHZ counterterms to retain finite-order renormalized amplitudes within the definability argument.

Reduce tensor integrals to scalar integrals, allowing shifted integer dimensions and propagator powers; use Schwinger parameters, Symanzik polynomials, and the Lee–Pomeransky polynomial G=U+F to obtain algebraic integral representations.
Substitute the full axionic redefinition into gauge and curvature coefficients; separately compare its saxionic partner with the printed expression.

Anomaly descent and bulk inflow are matched to worldsheet gravitational, transverse-rotation and gauge anomalies. Gauge matching includes classical Green–Schwarz contributions from scalars with gauged shifts.
Expand, decompose traces, and sum chirality-signed contributions before applying anomaly descent; mixed abelian charge products remain explicit.
Reduce the flux-independent brane volume action at quadratic derivative order, keeping frame factors, cycle volumes, and the compactification-scale hierarchy explicit.
Add the charged-Fermi budget 8k and the full potential scalar budget 4k−2.

Cartan reduction and matrix-rank subadditivity bound contributions from Fermi multiplets and axionic scalars. Microscopic tests employ dimensional reduction, geometric mode counting and index theorems.
Cancel bulk inflow against weakly coupled EFT-string worldsheet anomalies, subject to standard axionic couplings and a spectrum-minimality assumption.
Enumerate instanton actions, impose positivity, and use flux-compatible M2 attachments plus holomorphy for the wrapped-M5 contribution.
Bound each intersecting-stack indicator by its positive integer intersection, then use nonnegative bundle charge in the tadpole.

Start from the ten-dimensional equations, solve the form sector, and reduce the Einstein/dilaton equations to a one-dimensional action with a lapse multiplier. Its variation imposes a constraint propagated by the remaining equations.

For two exponential terms, construct an autonomous three-variable system with one constraint, compactify phase space, identify invariant surfaces and fixed points, and use linearization, endpoint series and numerical integration to reconstruct S(T).

Use Veff = V + Vone-loop + ΔVT + Vring, including SMEFT thermal effects and ring resummation. Determine critical minima by stationarity and degeneracy, and calculate O(3)-symmetric Euclidean bounce solutions numerically with AnyBubble.

Map Wilson coefficients into transition parameters and an imported acoustic-spectrum fit, then calculate SNRs and local Fisher confidence regions. The Fisher denominator includes signal and detector noise; a Galactic white-dwarf-binary foreground is added to the effective sensitivity.

Compute OuH effects using the fermionic universal one-loop effective action and covariant derivative expansion, compare the potential contribution with Coleman–Weinberg, and canonically normalize the Higgs through a field redefinition expanded to first order in the Wilson coefficients.

Use functional kernels and a resolvent identity to characterize the full propagator formally. An auxiliary Gaussian field replaces quadratic-in-H vertices with linear ones, organizing perturbative order without resolving the remaining computational complexity.

Compare vacuum-to-pair diagrams with Bogolyubov coefficients in solvable cosmologies and one-particle scattering with an adiabatic/WKB calculation. Apply LSZ to the exact conformal two-point function in the 1+1-dimensional example.

Split the exact quadratic action into a Minkowski free action and external-source interactions proportional to H, H² and Ḣ. Fourier transforms of coordinate powers generate momentum delta functions and their derivatives; ordinary flat-space propagators are retained.
Restrict the physically relevant parameter domain using the stated superradiance-avoidance condition ΩL<1, comparing its boundary with fixed-temperature horizon branches.

For AdS5 Kerr, exploit monotonic j(a) and the increasing r_H(a) on the large branch, allowing r_H to serve as a proxy for angular momentum. Eliminate a from the temperature equation to obtain the simpler rational expression for specific entropy in equation (36).

Compute entropy from horizon area and divide by physical mass. At fixed mass, use the first law to explain the entropy sign; at fixed temperature, eliminate mass with the horizon equation and study the resulting horizon-radius and specific-entropy functions.

Use the Narain charge lattice, mass formula and level matching to identify vectors becoming massless. Vanishing winding in decompactified directions leaves momentum towers of the higher-dimensional massless spectrum.

Identify algebra roots using junction intersection pairings and monodromy-invariant loops; combine this local analysis with global K3 degenerations. An explicit Weierstrass model and base blowup are supplied for the D16 limit.

Construct asymptotically conserved worldsheet currents, compute their OPEs, and extract zero-mode commutators by contour integration. Finite Wilson lines are accommodated by field redefinitions preserving the leading OPEs.

Average the classical attraxion equation of motion over oscillations in V ≈ ρH, treating expansion as negligible within each oscillation and then including the dilution of the Higgs bath in the averaged evolution.
Estimate metastable-vacuum decay with Euclidean bounce actions: a triangular approximation for tunnelling toward φ = 0 and a rectangular approximation for transitions between neighboring valleys.

Track nonadiabatic Higgs modes using ωk = √(k² + mH²) and the growth of ω̇k/ωk². Modes with k² < |mH²| undergo tachyonic amplification. An imported analytic number-density estimate includes suppression by the quartic-induced effective mass mH² + 3λ⟨H²⟩eff.

Express solitonic charges through a composite U(1) connection, evaluate the large-gauge ambiguity of its Chern–Simons integral, and construct explicit CP¹ configurations on a defect-punctured S⁴ to establish bordisms between point and line defects.

Identify invertible charges using reduced spin bordism. Construct noninvertible generators as three-dimensional spin-TQFT partition functions, treating nontrivial bundles in the auxiliary gauge-field path integral and examining defect fusion.

Abelian GLSM σ-vacuum equations determine discriminant components. Localized A-twisted or corresponding (0,2) correlators, evaluated using quantum restriction and residues, distinguish singularities affecting the whole displayed correlator sector from those affecting only a subsector.

Heterotic/F-theory duality, mirror maps and the Fourier–Mukai transform connect GLSM parameters to F-theory divisor volumes. Known perturbative α′ corrections then guide the embedding and coupling dependence of the inferred F-theory singularity.

Non-probabilistic, counterfactual comparison of explanations: vary initial conditions, appropriately similar dynamical maps, or remote-scale physical realizations and ask whether the explanatory connection persists. Dynamical maps are described as one-parameter groups carrying states between times.

Physical illustrations summarize Friedmann/scalar-field dynamics, quantum-field-theoretic calculation of perturbation spectra, and modified dispersion relations used to test ultraviolet sensitivity. These are explanatory applications of existing physics, not new technical derivations or independently checked calculations.

Construct the gradient using a block-diagonal superspace metric with a DeWitt−1 gravitational sector. Remove diffeomorphism and Maxwell gauge degeneracies using the DeTurck vector and Λ=τ∇αAα; the static principal parts become spatial diffusion operators.

Linear stability is treated as an eigenvalue problem using even pseudospectral discretization. Nonlinear flows use sixth-order spatial finite differences and second-order Crank–Nicholson time stepping with an iterative implicit solver. Spherical extremal near-horizon flows are also solved analytically using Lambert W.

Construct coordinate-invariant contractions cn of powers of the covariant Hessian of ln V with its gradient, together with traces dn. Express these in the kinematic frame and solve algebraic systems for ε and relations defining the attractor trajectory.

Project velocities along Killing directions, derive effective gradients for frozen fields, and linearize the reduced dynamics. Analyze block-matrix eigenvalues for backgrounds and apply the Routh–Hurwitz criterion to coupled superhorizon isocurvature perturbations.

Numerical spectra use the transport method in Inflation.jl, Bunch–Davies initial conditions eight e-folds before horizon exit, and five logarithmically spaced modes near the pivot. Differential evolution searches initial conditions and parameters for long-lived slow-roll, rapid-turn examples.

Quantize quadratic fluctuations with Neumann boundary conditions after mapping the strip to a finite interval. Treat the degenerate n=0 sector through a reduced two-dimensional action and finite-width corrections. Estimate boundary-layer effects by derivative-expansion power counting.

Use the Weyl-invariant Goldstone EFT S=α∫√g|∂χ|³+…; evaluate its current, stress tensor and charges on χ=μt+ℓφ. Expand charge integrals at narrow strip width and invert them perturbatively to obtain the equation of state.

Classify the finitely many form factors contributing to a process with fixed external content, reducing interaction monomials by partial integration, tensor symmetries and Bianchi identities. Construct amplitudes from tree diagrams with dressed propagators and vertices derived from Γ; these diagrams already incorporate its quantum corrections.

Use crossing symmetry and helicity decompositions, and project scalar s-channel amplitudes with aj(s) = (1/32π)∫[-1,1] dcosθ Pj(cosθ) As. The minimally coupled distinct-scalar example has nonzero exchange partial waves only at j = 0 and j = 2.

Review first-principles routes using truncated Wetterich flows, background heat-kernel methods and fluctuation correlation functions, together with reconstruction of effective-action form factors from CDT three-volume autocorrelations.
Flux backgrounds are organized using G-structures, SU(3) torsion classes, the generalized tangent bundle TM ⊕ T*M, and polyform pure-spinor differential equations.
The nonrelativistic torus example uses a βγ worldsheet system, winding-mode expansions and Virasoro constraints to obtain an asserted closed-string spectrum.
Worldsheet sigma-model actions, conformal gauge, vanishing metric/B-field/dilaton beta functions, and supersymmetry Killing-spinor conditions constrain internal geometry.

The curvature-entropy proposal uses an adapted Newman–Penrose null frame, Weyl scalar Ψ₂ and a first frame derivative DW of the Weyl tensor, with D=nᵃ∇ₐ. An integral involving DW/Ψ₂ extends from r=0 to the horizon.

The Hookean construction defines k through rotating versus nonrotating Hawking temperatures and sets x=r₊. Thermodynamic geometry uses the entropy Hessian in variables M and J and its scalar curvature.

The evaporation example combines the Hiscock–Weems treatment of Hawking emission and Schwinger discharge with a minimal dilaton correction C to the pair-production exponential; censorship constrains that correction.

Construct geometry from Abelian charge tables, complete-intersection superpotentials and D-/F-term constraints; identify coordinate patches, residual discrete gauge actions, divisors and triangulations. Shifted momenta of non-oscillator massless twisted states supply exceptional GLSM charges, using an imported construction.

Compare torsion-related theories in a common Fermi-superfield basis, retaining anomalous field-redefinition Jacobians. Combine residual gauge transformations with worldsheet flux quantization to extract phases; use logarithmic field-dependent FI terms for worldsheet Green–Schwarz cancellation of compact mixed anomalies.

Use the democratic RR formulation and axionic monodromies to impose global consistency of invariant field strengths. Anomaly-inflow-type source terms localized on the EFT string worldsheet identify electrically and magnetically charged modes.

Count multi-towers using approximately direct-product charge lattices. In w = 2 limits, independently scan D2 multi-wrapping and induced D0 charge, justified using fluxes and non-Abelian Wilson lines on the elliptic fibre. In w = 1 limits, include fluxed D4/D2/D0 configurations.

Compute hypermultiplet threshold corrections IIR_AB = IUV_AB − (8/3π²)∑qA qB log(Λsp/m), counting states below Λsp = MP/√Stot. Compare their leading asymptotic powers with the known large-volume gauge kinetic matrix.

The QSC uses QQ-relations, asymptotic charges, branch-cut analyticity and gluing conditions to determine spectral dimensions. Appendix C outlines a hybrid perturbative approach: solve a fourth-order Baxter equation at leading order, then iterate finite-difference equations using η-functions.

Implement orbifolding by invariant-state projection plus added twisted sectors. Use a twisted monodromy AT(z) on the string side and twist insertions in traces or boundary phases in nested Bethe–Yang equations on the spin-chain side.

Double Wick rotation converts spatial twists into mirror-theory chemical potentials. Canonical TBA is reduced to local Y-system and Hirota T-system equations; this reduction discards constant twist data, which must be restored through asymptotic conditions.

Regular triangulations arise from height lifting and lower-hull projection. The fast sampler perturbs Delaunay heights with Gaussian noise and rejects non-fine triangulations; the slower sampler combines height-space walks with bistellar flips preserving fineness and regularity.

Ambient intersections of distinct divisors come from fan-cone data; self-intersections follow from divisor linear equivalences using facet-based sparsity and sparse Cholesky decomposition. Cone routines use nonnegative least squares for ray redundancy and quadratic programming to minimize |x|² subject to Mx ≥ c.

Lattice-point enumeration first applies LLL reduction to shrink a bounding box, then scans integer coordinate slices and reverses the transformation. Stored saturated facet inequalities support recursive face construction through facet intersections and affine-dimension tests.

Quantize transverse circular polarizations in Coulomb gauge and analyze Fλ″+[k²+a²m²±k df/dτ]Fλ=0 through Mathieu instabilities and Floquet growth. For constant frequency the quoted narrow-band estimates include q=γk/ω and μ≈γ/2.

Match the resonance-generated density to the paper's adopted present abundance, 9.6×10^−48 GeV⁴. Evolve momenta by a^−1 and energy density by a^−4 until physical momentum reaches m, then by a^−3; require the matter-like transition before equality, using Tm>10^−9 GeV.

An unbounded F_{8−p} flux is exchanged for N Dp domain walls wrapped on (p+2−D)-cycles. Harmonic superposition gives schematic metric and dilaton powers; internal volume and the D-dimensional Planck length then yield c ∼ (R_AdS/l_p,D)^(D−2). These powers are compared with scalar-potential scalings.
The shift-symmetry argument combines the AdS mass–dimension equation m²R² = Δ(Δ−d), known free-field polynomial-shift masses, and the near-boundary expansion φ ∼ φ₀z⁻ᵏ + φ₁zᵏ⁺ᵈ.

Differentiate Einstein equations along λ and use metric-variation identities for curvature to derive the required stress-tensor flow. Specialize to Ricci–Bourguignon flow; analyze its flat-background linearization using harmonic gauge.

Use volume-preserving entropy-functional gradient flows, including a recipe attributed to prior work that starts from the Euclidean string-frame action. Reduce spacetime-constant configurations to coupled ODEs and solve selected examples numerically.

Reviewed axiomatic tools include Wightman and Haag–Kastler systems, bordism-functor formulations and factorization algebras. The latter assign chain complexes to open sets with a multiplicative cosheaf structure.

Borel resummation, trans-series and Lefschetz thimbles organize divergent expansions. Exact WKB and spectral networks connect BPS counting with Darboux coordinates and reconstruction of nonabelian flat connections from spectral-cover data.

Supersymmetric localization, Ω-deformation and Coulomb-branch u-plane integrals relate protected observables and four-manifold invariants to modular/mock modular functions. BPS wall crossing also motivates TBA-type integral equations constructing hyperkähler metrics.

Analytic radial solutions and integrals use incomplete Beta functions, harmonic numbers, and generalized hypergeometric functions. Generic-mass AdS5 scalar exchange is treated numerically with δ=0, shooting from the smooth center and matching boundary asymptotics.

Following an earlier effective-potential method, the authors classically integrate out photon, graviton, and neutral-scalar fluctuations using linearized equations. Their nonlocal quartic effective interactions allow exchange contributions to be evaluated through first-order Hamiltonian perturbation theory.

Generalized dark matter parameterizes EDE through fluid density, pressure, sound speed, and viscosity in its gravitational stress tensor. Mapping scalar models into this description helps avoid numerical difficulties from widely separated oscillation and expansion timescales in Boltzmann calculations.

CMB inference fits numerical temperature/polarization power spectra simultaneously for cosmological parameters. The heuristic account integrates c_s/H before last scattering for the sound horizon and the expansion history afterward for distance; higher acoustic peaks constrain physical baryon and matter densities.

The local ladder uses geometric distances to calibrate Cepheids, Cepheids to calibrate SN Ia luminosities, and standardized Hubble-flow SN Ia to infer H0. The review discusses covariance modeling, null tests, and analysis variants rather than presenting a new measurement.

Along Z=Z*, requiring V=0 reduces the superpotential problem to d(log W0)/dZ=±√(3gK)−KZ. The two branches are integrated and combined; multi-field constructions use a product ansatz and separated equations with coefficients constrained by a sphere.

The authors derive canonically normalized scalar and fermion spectra and compare their supertraces with curvature formulae. Kähler transformations and a disk-to-half-plane coordinate change are used to relate alternative descriptions.

Invariant flux automatically solves the non-invariant F-terms on the symmetric locus. Stabilization is then bounded using the rank of the linearized F-term matrix, split into a holomorphic Hessian block and a metric-times-W0 block.

A Mathematica scan computes maximal Hessian ranks from symmetry-allowed monomial products and relations modulo the Jacobi ideal. In favorable cases mirror symmetry reduces the invariant-sector flux problem to a few-modulus calculation.

Reduce Abelian 7d Chern–Simons theory on surfaces and handlebodies, using Wilson-surface linking and quantum-torus relations. Handlebody surgery is translated into 5d condensation defects and their topological boundaries.

Solve F(Ω)=Ω for enhanced surface symmetries, then find invariant rank-g isotropic subspaces through F^T K_L=K_L Q, Q∈GL(g,F_p). The arithmetic uses cyclotomic factorization, splitting fields, Jordan blocks and the symplectic intersection form.

The authors modify the BSSN-based GRChombo package for 3+1 numerical relativity. Initial conformal metric and trace-free extrinsic curvature are set to δij and zero; the conformal factor is relaxed to enforce the Hamiltonian constraint.

Diagnostics include scalar-field profiles, extrinsic curvature K, an apparent-horizon finder, and wall-crossing profiles of the longitudinal expansion HL=−u^i u^j Kij and proper-distance factor γ. The wall-width estimate is compared with HL^{-1}.

Parameterized Dirac observables represent gauge-dependent triads and metric components on the physical Hilbert space. Functional parameters select coordinates/slicings; the ordered-label observable Ô(z) supplies the radial triad, and the Hamiltonian constraint supplies Eφ.

Replace Kφ by sin(ρKφ)/ρ. The basic prescription fixes small dimensionless ρ; improved dynamics instead imposes 4πℓPl² k_j ρ̄_j² = Δ, associating the point holonomy with the LQG area gap. Relabeling vertex states makes improved holonomies act by unit shifts.

A linear combination of Hamiltonian and radial diffeomorphism constraints eliminates Kx and gives a Hamiltonian with vanishing self-bracket. Loop quantization uses one-dimensional spin networks; group averaging implements radial diffeomorphisms while preserving vertex order.

The structure-growth explanation uses the post-decoupling Newtonian equation δ̈m=−2Hδ̇m+4πGρ̄mδm for minimally interacting pressureless baryons and CDM, with δb≈δc. The comparison assumes common early matter-background initial conditions constrained by the CMB.

Authors use CLASS with Monte Python for correlated MCMC samples, GetDist for posterior analysis and MCEvidence for approximate Bayesian evidences. Model comparisons use evidence ratios and a revised Jeffreys scale; parameter tables generally report 68% confidence intervals.

Amplitude techniques include recursive tree constructions, unitarity-based construction of loop amplitudes, geometric representations, and color–kinematics duality. The double copy constructs gravitational amplitudes by replacing gauge-theory color factors with kinematic factors.

Computational methods include Euclidean lattice Monte Carlo and Hamiltonian quantum simulation. Quantum approaches require field-space digitization, state preparation, and approximate evolution such as Trotterization, with truncation errors and resource requirements still requiring systematic study.

Reviewed bootstrap methods include convex optimization of conformal constraints, analytic Lorentzian methods, and optimization of S-matrices subject to analyticity, unitarity, and Lorentz invariance. Hamiltonian truncation numerically diagonalizes deformed theories.

Positive cones of weakly coupled scalar, axion, spin-two and QED-like amplitudes identify unbounded directions. Adjustable masses allow independent positive combinations at dimension 8 and dimension 10, or dimension 8 and dimension 12.

Forward crossing dispersion relations express coefficient combinations as absorptive integrals. Positivity bounds the quadratic coefficients; explicit infrared subtraction is needed for fourth-order coefficients.

Crossing-symmetric conformal-ρ expansions with χ prefactors encode helicity kinematics. Wigner-d partial waves turn nonlinear unitarity into positive-semidefinite matrix constraints, optimized using Mathematica and SDPB.

Couple the non-invertible current minimally to b̃ and promote the auxiliary scalar to a four-dimensional integration variable. Its Lagrange-multiplier equation imposes db̃∧da=0; the coupling also contains −b̃∧a∧da/(8π²).

The appendix defines Chern–Simons integrals using gauge patches and overlap terms on S¹×S². Bulk and overlap contributions are equal in the winding calculation, producing the factor of two required for the stated flux projection.

Gauge-average the conserved defect operator using a suitably normalized compact-scalar path integral on its three-manifold. Summing scalar winding sectors produces magnetic-flux projectors; auxiliary Chern–Simons fields are integrated out to compare rational-angle constructions.

Use a Lagrange multiplier for the FLRW curvature relation to construct a point-like vacuum Lagrangian on minisuperspace {a,R}. Apply Noether invariance and conserved quantities, then solve the Euler–Lagrange equations together with the zero-energy constraint EL=0.

Employ conformal scalar-field reformulation, effective curvature density and pressure, cosmographic energy-condition tests, slow-roll parameters, and swampland potential criteria. The printed conformal definitions include ω=(1/2)ln|fR| and V=(f−R fR)/(2 fR²); their signs and normalization are retained as source conventions.

Recast the matter cosmology as an autonomous first-order system using N=ln a, x1=−dot(fR)/(H fR), x2=−f/(6 fR H²), and Ωm=ρm/(3 fR H²). Matter-era initial conditions and subsequent numerical integration are described as a route to observational comparison.

Uses the imported Cartier–DeWitt-Morette integrator construction on Banach field spaces, with affine extensions to prescribed boundary data; analyzes norms and homotopy classes of metric configurations.
Uses local blow-ups, boundary geodesics and exponential maps to construct proposed minimal worldsheets, followed by an appeal to Kontsevich quantization of Poisson manifolds.
The scalar example uses Sommerfeld wedge diffraction, Helmholtz separation and mode quantization. Cosmological arguments use zeta regularization and inverse-Laplace saddle points.

Topological defects with three-dimensional Chern–Simons theories, Witten-effect actions on magnetic lines, and defect fusion diagnose non-invertibility. One-loop RG evolution connects infrared Z′ parameters to UV gauge effects.

Yukawa diagonalization and triangle-anomaly bookkeeping identify surviving symmetries. Instanton fermion zero modes determine ’t Hooft vertices; charged-lepton Yukawa insertions convert these into neutrino mass operators.

Holographic analysis uses folding, two ETW branes, wedge holography, and entropies of T T̄-deformed CFTs. The imported island prescription is Sgen(R)=min extr∂I[Area(∂I)/(4GN)+SEE(I∪R)]; its application to transition actions is the authors' interpretation.

FMP uses canonical momenta, Hamiltonian and momentum constraints, wall junction conditions, an effective turning-point potential, and Hamilton–Jacobi integration of bulk and brane actions. The authors interpret imposing the Hamiltonian constraint as a microcanonical description.

Euclidean instanton/background subtraction; Weyl transformations remove either the dilaton kinetic term or the Ricci coupling. The AP constraints allow a CDL-type calculation without the thin-wall approximation; a separate thin-wall calculation and an ADM boundary term connect to BT.

Minimize the moduli potentials and transform the input counting measure using Jacobians, retaining implicit moduli dependence. KKLT replaces (W0,y) with (m3/2,Λ) at fixed S; LVS replaces (s,y) at fixed W0,C0. Analytic expansions are supplemented by reported numerical density evaluations.

Imported statistical inputs are a flat distribution for complex W0, axio-dilaton measure dS/s², and throat measure dy/[y(ln y)²], where y=|z|^(4/3). Their factorized combination is dN=η|W0| d|W0| dS dy/[s² y(ln y)²]. These are inputs reviewed by the paper, not newly established distributions.
Circle KK reduction and expansion of the induced brane action produce vector kinetic, mass and SM stress-energy interactions. The combination Xμ+∂μYθ implements absorption of the branon.

Inflationary gravitational-production calculations are adapted to the modified brane expansion and tensor spectrum; α-attractor reheating relations connect CMB quantities to the gravitational-wave reheating frequency.

Use normalized Euclidean weights and both orientations of relative entropy. For the non-interacting reference, Ig=I0+gII gives ⟨II⟩NI ≥ WT−WNI ≥ ⟨II⟩T at g=1. Reference choices also include massive free fields, infinite heavy mass, and a thermal construction.

Combine tree-level saddle approximations and one-loop effective actions with field redefinitions removing heavy-field linear terms and light kinetic corrections. Constant-gradient scalar backgrounds and suitable constant gauge field strengths isolate selected higher-derivative operators.

Coherence strictification and graphical calculus support induction of right modules into bimodules. Relative tensor products supply module monoidality; the monoidal free-module functor and splitting of condensation monads supply duals.

The symmetric fermionic analysis encodes the Picard 2-category by a fibre sequence of spectra, reduces extension data to SH⁷(E[4]), and uses spectral sequences, product splitting, and Cauchy completion.

Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequences compute supercohomology and super-Witt cohomology. The displayed d2 operations use Sq² and its exponentiation; bosonic Galois descent introduces the twisted operation Sq²X + ι₂X.
Specify the observable data first, then construct an action reproducing either local expectation values or low-energy boundary amplitudes and correlators.
Choose asymptotically stationary particle labels, remove external propagation, and evaluate the limiting correlators in those labels.
Integrate the comoving group velocity to decide whether particles retain position labels or can propagate to arbitrarily large comoving distances.
Expand the interacting Fourier-space integral with its displacement sources, preserving the denominator needed to remove terms disconnected from the inserted field.

The separate-coupling, five-variable resummation in section 4.1 is rejected because it produces arbitrary and momentum-conservation-dependent nonperturbative factors. The revised treatment resums the combined coupling g = g1 g2 g3.
Collapse each interaction sector onto one momentum, close the final momentum by conservation, and compute a first-order real Gaussian toy integral.
Select the coincident-momentum pattern for repeated factors of one flux representative while retaining the distinct mode integration measures.
Transform a growth-controlled asymptotic expansion, specify singularity-avoiding contours, and add ambiguity-cancelling nonperturbative sectors before interpreting the completed expectation value.
Organize real-component mode integrals by equal-momentum patterns, evaluate their Gaussian moments, and sum the resulting nodal contributions with consistent normalization.

Generalized Borel transformation, analytic continuation and Laplace integration are applied to Gevrey series. The mathematical discussion explicitly notes that the Gevrey bound alone guarantees neither the required continuation nor convergence of the Laplace integral.
Configuration-space path integrals about displaced interacting vacua are organized into nodal diagrams. Hermite-polynomial expansions parametrize the initially unknown displacement functions.
Expand an excited state in configuration eigenstates, evaluate diagonal terms directly, and retain derivative-dependent evolution before summing the weighted components.
Absorb linear momentum dependence into the source profile, exclude propagator-changing quadratic terms, and evaluate the remaining displacement on the interacting vacuum.

Generalize the Euclidean Ward-identity proof: integrate charge on a surrounding sphere, differentiate the defect with respect to its continuous label, and use radius independence and spherical symmetry to obtain an R^−3 current–operator correlator.

Establish topological invariance of the added dθ∧F coupling through a background two-form source b and Z[b]=Z[b+dΛ]. An exact source localized on a regulated hypersurface makes independence of its location explicit.

Exact redefinitions of A and B produce a two-derivative action. The authors vary this action to obtain effective matter sources and Friedmann equations, then solve the tensionless equations and expand selected solutions in 1/α′.

Integrate out F+ recursively in α′, using projections defined by S. Integration by parts and perturbative field redefinitions remove higher derivatives, dilaton derivatives and Tr L² terms; induced α′⁴ contributions from α′² redefinitions must be retained.

The authors use radial equations of motion and Green functions for the force, the two-derivative fake-superpotential gradient flow for the mass, and the attractor mechanism with Iyer–Wald entropy for horizon corrections.

Three- and four-derivative operator classification uses Bianchi identities, commutators of covariant derivatives, integration by parts, and derivative field redefinitions implementing leading equations of motion.

Nonrelativistic WIMP–nucleus scattering is organized through a velocity expansion in effective field theory. The report emphasizes spin-dependent interactions requiring nonzero nuclear spin and spin-independent interactions often coherently enhanced for large-A targets.

Gravitational-wave standard sirens combine luminosity distances from compact-binary mergers with redshifts to infer the distance–redshift relation and H0 without a cosmic distance ladder. Stochastic-background spectra can probe early phase transitions and topological defects.

Inflationary observables include two-point correlations and power spectra, CMB B-mode polarization, and three-point correlations/bispectra. Triangle configurations and their scale dependence are used to characterize primordial interactions and additional degrees of freedom.

Use the probe DBI plus Wess–Zumino action with constant dilaton. Legendre transformations replace internal angular velocity by conserved angular momentum and produce a radial Hamiltonian, including couplings to the bulk gauge field and RR potential.

Compare Hamiltonian dynamics with Israel thin-shell junction conditions expanded in the probe regime. Matching requires a charge-dependent effective tension accounting for dissolved flux, rather than a constant-tension shell alone.

Evaluate environmental correlators with distributional coincidence singularities; regulate ultraviolet integrals using a dimensional-regularization variant. Compare divergent Hamiltonian terms with the momentum/time dependence allowed by gravitational EFT counterterms.

A projection onto the environmental Bunch-Davies vacuum produces a Nakajima-Zwanzig memory equation, truncated at second order in the system-environment interaction. Linearity in the system field permits separate mode evolution at this order.

Jointly expand the system-field and density-matrix factors multiplying the environmental kernel to obtain late-time Lindblad evolution. Gaussian density matrices are then treated through covariance transport equations and Green-function solutions.

The matrix program uses a high-temperature Matsubara expansion, ordered temporal eigenvalues, spatial submatrix traces and a proposed length-to-metric prescription. Thermal partition-function derivatives supply stress-tensor correlations for scalar and tensor fluctuations.

The heterotic analysis dimensionally reduces the ten-dimensional effective action, stabilizes the four-dimensional dilaton by gaugino condensation, uses W=W0−Ae^(−a0S) and a standard Kähler potential, and integrates out axio-dilaton fluctuations.

Removes scalar phases from fermion masses by chiral field redefinitions, integrates derivative-current terms by parts, and invokes the axial triangle anomaly to infer gluon and photon couplings. These are manuscript calculations around its assumed vacuum.

Integrates out Δ and Ω to obtain effective scalar operators, parametrizes the four light scalars by radial fields and phases, and expands the phase-dependent potential around assumed VEVs. Orthogonal transformations separate eaten modes from a two-field pseudo-Goldstone mass matrix.

Uses the reviewed vertical-flux formalism G4 = φIJ[DI]∧[DJ], with integer coefficients in the chosen divisor-product lattice. Integrated fluxes satisfy Θiα = −κij(Σ·Dα·Dβ)φjβ. Here κij is the inverse Killing metric, which generally differs from the Cartan matrix outside ADE.

Optimizes linear charge expressions over quantized flux choices subject to a quadratic tadpole bound. The geometric strategy combines a large Euler characteristic with small intersection numbers on the gauge divisor; an SU(3) → U(1) example first illustrates the construction.

Finds surviving U(1) generators through null vectors piΘiα = 0 for every α, excluding combinations aligned with roots. Calculates charges by decomposing nonabelian representations and computes chiral indices from weights and integrated fluxes; bulk adjoints use KΣ by adjunction.

Identify candidate symmetries through currents and charge operators, requiring conservation, gauge invariance and single-valuedness. Couple localized D3-particle brane currents to violate current conservation, schematically dJ^(P)=-j.

Use nilpotent-orbit periods, mixed Hodge structures and the SL(2)-approximated Hodge star to reconstruct asymptotic gauge couplings. Hodge-norm growth estimates control physical D3 charges, with Q_q²=(1/2)||q||².

CYJAX uses JAX jit compilation, vmap vectorization, automatic differentiation, and symbolically generated expressions. A computational graph exposes intermediate geometric quantities; explicit metric and curvature implementations can also be compared with repeated automatic differentiation.

A Flax network predicts Cholesky parameters for H from moduli. Training samples batches of moduli and manifold points, evaluates a weighted Monge-Ampère residual, differentiates through the metric computation, and updates network parameters by gradient descent.

Generate manifold samples by intersecting X with random projective lines p+tq, solving Q(p+tq)=0. Monte Carlo integration corrects the known induced Fubini-Study sampling measure dA using weights w=dvol/dA, with dvol obtained from the holomorphic top form.

Explicit coframe exterior calculus and generalized spin connections determine G2 torsion projections. The G2 cross product constructs almost-contact endomorphisms and the third vector field from two orthogonal unit vectors.
Contact-form ansätze are treated using numerical parameter choices and expansions around finite N0. Transverse forms are obtained by solving i_R Ω− = 0 and the decomposition *7Φ = −σ∧Ω− + (1/2)ωΦ∧ωΦ.

Construct constant-flux frames using doubled-group adjoint actions, Maurer–Cartan forms and a locally defined WZW B-field. Constant-flux Bianchi identities become Lie-algebra Jacobi constraints; a further differential equation fixes the generalised dilaton up to a constant.

Adapt the Poláček–Siegel construction to general F: auxiliary group coordinates geometrise the connection on a nonphysical mega-space. Its generalised frame contains the physical frame, spin connection and an antisymmetric Poláček–Siegel field.

Use the flux formulation of generalised geometry, expressing the action through generalised fluxes and projectors. Expand retained fields in tensors invariant under the generalised structure group F; intrinsic torsion controls the resulting gauge action.

Gauge EoM-based symmetries with nondynamical backgrounds, expand the topological action on an auxiliary (2n+1)-manifold, and recursively choose Chern–Weil counterterms and gauge-invariant field strengths to cancel operator-valued extension ambiguities.

Represent symmetry generators and charged defects by distributional background fields. Relate configurations through gauge transformations and compute the accompanying anomaly phase on a mapping torus; linking numbers then determine charges and correlation identities.
Initialize each Fourier mode in the early adiabatic vacuum, integrate through background nonadiabaticity, and extract a settled occupation in the late adiabatic regime.
Convert produced comoving number into today's nonrelativistic density through pre-reheating expansion, radiation matching and post-reheating entropy conservation.
The paper applies dominant-term interval matching to a minimally coupled light scalar in idealized de Sitter and kination backgrounds; its printed boundaries require correction.
Use abundance and a positive infrared particle-spectrum slope as a proxy for CMB isocurvature safety, without evaluating the full normalized density convolution.
Background integration and PyTransport perturbation evolution determine the benchmark observables; no numerical computation has been independently reproduced here.

Decompose perturbations into spherical harmonics, solve static radial equations perturbatively with horizon regularity, and identify growing tidal-source and decaying response terms at infinity. Match gauge-invariant fields to worldline operators.

For axial metric perturbations, use Regge–Wheeler gauge and an auxiliary gauge-invariant field χ, integrate out constrained fields, and obtain a sourced Regge–Wheeler equation. Higher derivatives are reduced using the zeroth-order equation.
Construct corrected charged backgrounds through O(α), extract asymptotic electric charge and ADM mass, and evaluate their relation in the extremal limit.

Use the symmetry-preserving Papadopoulos–Tseytlin ansatz and linearized nonsupersymmetric KS deformations. Conjugate variables ξi organize first-order equations; nested-integral solutions admit UV/IR expansions and numerical matching.

Compute the canonically normalized D7 gaugino mass from a localized flux–holomorphic-form integral. Compare with four-dimensional supergravity using the GVW superpotential, omitting the nonperturbative D7 term because it was absent from the flux calculation.

Decompose the perturbed complex three-form into (p,q) components using the zeroth-order KS complex structure. Extract UV radial falloffs and interpret them through the holographic operator dictionary.

Calculate differential Drell–Yan observables at NNLO QCD using an amended MCFM-v9.0 implementation containing the model charges, Z′ contribution and interference. The authors report agreement within 1% against DY-Turbo and FEWZ; this pass does not independently validate that comparison.

Diagonalise the neutral gauge-boson mass matrix from two Higgs doublets and a singlet. Rotate the abelian coupling matrix to triangular form, encoding kinetic mixing in g_KM; modify the mass matrix and vector/axial fermion couplings accordingly.

Use CT18NNLO proton PDFs with uncertainties at 90% confidence level. Estimate scale uncertainty by a seven-point variation of renormalisation and factorisation scales up and down by factors of two, taking the envelope.

The ACV approach starts in the Regge limit, transforms to impact parameter and resums factorized genus contributions into an operator eikonal. Fourier transforms, partial waves and stationary-phase estimates relate impact-parameter and fixed-angle descriptions.

The review compares oscillator-state counting and the leading Hagedorn entropy with the black hole area law. Thermal backgrounds are estimated by saddles of a dimensionally reduced Euclidean effective action containing the winding mode.

Gross–Mende worldsheets are reviewed as K-sheeted sphere covers with N branch points, genus G = (K−1)(N−2)/2 and a two-dimensional electrostatic interpretation. Dominant-genus estimates and an imported Borel-resummability result organize the high-energy amplitude.

Uses cobordism, Baas–Sullivan manifolds with singularities, and the Adams spectral sequence. In the prime-two cobar resolution, the displayed d1 connects w1 to ξ1, representing two equally oriented points; the E1 page depends on the resolution.
Choose background structures, enumerate surviving cobordism classes, and distinguish restrictions that gauge their operators from defects that break the associated symmetry.
Cut a disk through a parity wall and reglue its faces with orientation reversal, then assess the quantum-state and energetic consequences.
Connect two I-folds by a regulator-sized crosscap tube instead of cutting a macroscopic disk; the exterior remains orientable and lacks distant parity holonomy.

Uses twisted backgrounds and locality, Poincaré duality, and codimension-two gravitational boundary conditions ∂X = C × Σ. The permitted normal-bundle generalization does not change the authors' conclusion.

Numerically integrate Lorentzian and Euclidean scalar–Friedmann equations from time-symmetric initial conditions. Scan a simple potential family for acceleration and tune plateau potentials to reproduce specified background expansion histories.

Reconstruct scalar kinetic and potential energies parametrically from H and ΩM when radiation is neglected. For wCDM, fit the reconstructed potential over the observed redshift interval and use a shooting method to obtain a future time-symmetric point.

In N = 1 supergravity with one chiral multiplet and canonical Kähler potential, factor the potential equation into first-order factors. Solve a linear auxiliary ODE and construct a superpotential expansion in inverse powers of an integration constant C.

Use collective-breaking spurions and operator-dimension counting: several low-dimensional interactions can carry a large combined PQ charge while requiring fewer inverse Planck powers. The paper acknowledges earlier discussion of this counting for composite axions.

Use flavor invariants built from fermion mass and axion-Yukawa matrices to diagnose tadpoles. In the specified vectorlike chain, invariants through k=m−2 vanish; the first potentially nonzero invariant has k=m−1 and polynomial degree 2m.

Integrate out heavy scalars at tree level and evaluate fermion-induced one-loop Coleman–Weinberg potentials. Compare the resulting PQ-breaking coefficients with the fully Planck-suppressed potential at fixed lowest allowed operator dimension n.

The argument combines holographic stress-tensor/current two-point-function scaling, the large-radius flat-space limit, and matching to maximal ungauged supergravity. Vanishing coupling abelianizes the nonabelian field strengths.

Use HKLL reconstruction and generalized-free-field oscillators to express the free bulk scalar ANEC as a positive coefficient times ∫du A†A. Null integration eliminates the pair-creation and pair-annihilation terms.

Integrate the Raychaudhuri and Einstein equations along initially parallel null probes. Negative transverse Green functions relate positive averaged null energy to time delay; higher-curvature effects enter through a graviton pseudotensor.

Apply a conformal Casimir to geodesic/Witten-diagram Regge OPEs, removing stress-tensor exchange and exposing bulk light-ray sources. Evaluate extensions with impact-parameter amplitudes and conformal Regge saddle points and pole residues.

Spectral arguments use Cheeger energy, Dirichlet forms, Rayleigh quotients and isoperimetric constants. The diameter bound uses L¹ optimal-transport localization into weighted geodesic intervals, followed by one-dimensional spectral inequalities.

Formal Otto calculus computes entropy derivatives along Wasserstein geodesics using continuity and Hamilton–Jacobi equations. Weighted Bochner/Raychaudhuri identities connect these derivatives to weighted Ricci curvature; Shannon and Tsallis entropies serve different equations.

The quadratic vacuum equations are separated into axionic and saxionic systems after showing W is real on shell. Matrix image/kernel conditions and the generalized inverse M⁺ organize flux constraints, flat directions and Q′ = Q − ½LᵀM⁺L.

Mass calculations use a symplectic flux decomposition, vielbeins for canonical normalization and eigenvalues of Z†Z, where Z_AB = e^(K/2)D_AD_BW. A direct scalar-potential Hessian calculation provides an alternative treatment of the axionic masses and separates axionic from saxionic modes.

A restricted saxion ansatz tⁱ = t̂f_Aⁱ + t̃Sⁱʲh_jᴮ gives two analytically tractable branches. A singular-M branch yields a sixth-order equation treated perturbatively near LCS; the aligned t̃ = 0 branch reduces to a cubic.

The one-loop input comes from a modular-invariant Z2 orbifold partition function on R9×S1, integrated over the torus fundamental domain. At the self-dual radius its normalization gives Λ=λgs²/α′ with λ≈0.705; dimensional reduction supplies the three-dimensional loop potential.

Scalar fluctuations are expanded in spherical harmonics and reduced to free sectors and a seven-scalar coupled mass matrix. The analysis adapts an imported supersymmetric spectrum calculation; small-coupling corrections are analytical, while the general loop-corrected eigenvalues are treated numerically.

Dimensional reduction to three dimensions and a Weyl transformation produce an Einstein-frame scalar potential. A total derivative required by the electric-flux variational problem reverses the naive electric contribution's sign; this term is essential to dilaton stabilization.

Fit theoretical PK parameters using a sum of squared uncertainty-normalized residuals for quantities including periastron advance, period decay, Einstein/Shapiro delays and mass ratio. Reported mass priors are uniform on [0,3] solar masses; conformal-only and conformal-plus-disformal models are analysed separately.

Use a scalar multipole expansion after integrating out short-distance fields. Obtain dissipative forces by integration by parts in orbit-averaged energy loss, reduce higher derivatives using Newtonian trajectories, and apply Gauss equations to secular orbital evolution.

Reduce the conservative two-body Lagrangian to centre-of-mass motion using conserved energy and angular momentum. Construct quasi-Keplerian trajectories through anomaly parametrisation, the Binet variable 1/r, radial turning points and perturbative expansion of orbital integrals.

Local thermodynamic stability is tested by positivity of the four principal minors of the energy Hessian in variables (S,Pz,J1,J2), with electric and magnetic charges fixed. A first-law quadratic-form identity permits evaluation using (a,b,rh,e^δ3), imposing the fixed-charge differential constraints before setting a=b.

The calculation is performed in the IIA frame. Its paired Lorentz Chern-Simons terms cancel the frame ambiguities or singularities encountered in a direct heterotic evaluation. The authors use the on-shell duality relation, including its additional term, to transfer the entropy correction between frames.

An imported thermodynamic shortcut obtains the leading entropy correction at fixed conserved quantities by evaluating the four-derivative action on the uncorrected solution. The corrected spacetime solution need not be constructed for this calculation; rh, a and δ1 are then implicit functions of the conserved quantities.

Potential extrema are examined through plotted V(T) and V′(T). Numerical integration of the potential integral is used as an additional comparison with the analytical estimate; dimensional reduction and Higgs-field rescaling separately estimate gravitational and visible-brane mass scales.

The radion potential is obtained by inserting the warped ansatz into the bulk action and integrating over the extra dimension. The analytical estimate drops the α-dependent correction in the warp exponential relative to the RS part and expresses the result using an exponential integral and coefficient functions.

The bulk f(R) equations are expanded using A(y)=ky+αA1(y) and B(y)=1+αB1(y), retaining first order in α. The resulting equations determine the reported corrections, and Z2 symmetry is then imposed to obtain leading corrections to the brane tensions.
Match pole and zero sets so crossed-channel singularities cancel in residues, then choose equally spaced towers; positivity remains an independent test.
Test the full dressed expression for both pole cancellation and polynomial residues; vanishing tachyon residues alone do not justify arbitrary denominator additions.
Take pole residues, recouple internal representations, project onto angular polynomials, and intersect nonnegativity constraints; retain the distinction between this test and full unitarity.
Iteratively promote inferred exchanged states to external states and impose further amplitude consistency; the required amplitudes are future inputs.
Resolve crossed-channel projectors into the residue channel before imposing coefficient positivity; keep external representations and basis normalizations fixed.
Assuming the imported positive F⁴ decomposition for D≤10, require scalar-factor positivity as a sufficient test; this need not characterize the full allowed space.

Concrete stabilization examples use the linear dilaton multiplet: the kinetic functions satisfy ℓg′=-ℓf′+f. A chosen exponential ansatz for f determines g through incomplete gamma functions, with g(0)=0, and is inserted into the scalar potential.

The no-go arguments impose positive energy and stationarity, eliminate superpotential derivatives, and use a negative complex mixed second derivative to establish an unstable Hessian direction. Factorization or fixed-point modular symmetry supplies the required Hessian block structure.

At Θ(k)=0, the bulk and brane null directions align and β vanishes at the anchor. Interior β≥0 then fixes the sign of its inward normal derivative, giving ∂λΘ(k)=-∂nβ/ℓS≤0. A corresponding α boundary argument proves the companion inequality.

Vary the holographic extremal-surface area under null boundary deformations. The normal deformation αk̄+βℓ̄ obeys a cooperative elliptic system; an imported strong-positivity theorem propagates nonnegative boundary data into the surface, conditional on a suitable supersolution.
